| RT-209 | Codex-architecture-deepen port, row 3 (found 2026-11-01) | **DEFECT CLOSED iter-1635, with the kill switch fixed at iter-1645 and the consumer STILL deferred** (the type-level orphan is gone: every public type here has a production construction site, pinned by a source guard. Two things remain open and both are named below rather than implied: no subscriber READS `TurnEnd::attribution`, and the 'kill switch' was unreachable from `operant.toml` until iter-1645). Original finding: **OPEN**: `crates/operant-core/src/turn_attribution.rs` (409 LOC at the time of the finding, 712 by iter-1655: `TurnSpan`, `SpanDuration`, `TurnBreakdown`, `TurnAttribution`) is exported at `lib.rs` and called by NOTHING, tests included. It shipped as a dead module, and its own doc header called itself "the RT-199 fix", which is FALSE: RT-199 closed at iter-1505 through `agent/mod.rs`'s `tool_durations_by_call` map (see the RT-199 row above). The false claim was the expensive half and is corrected in the module header as of this row. What remains open is the emission site the plan specified: build the four-span exclusive breakdown and render it on the volatile `<turn_context>` tail beside `<context_budget>` (`agent/run.rs`). **The plan's specified seat was wrong and iter-1626 measured why**: the volatile `<turn_context>` tail is built by `build_messages` ONCE, before the loop starts (`agent/run.rs` -> `build_turn_context` -> `build_messages`, which the loop only appends to), so at that moment no model call has happened and no tool has run. A block placed there renders `n/a` forever, which is the RT-199 failure wearing a new hat. iter-1626 is the probe commit that measured this and reverted the attempt. **iter-1631 ships option 1 instead — emit at turn END, off the request path**: `TurnEnd.attribution: Option<TurnBreakdown>` (`turn_end.rs`) filled by `OperantAgent::turn_attribution()` from `turn_start.elapsed()` + the folded `llm_duration` + `turn_tool_duration()`, with `user_wait` honestly `Unmeasured` (the approval gate is a synchronous decision and the guardian LLM's time already sits inside `inference`). `AgentConfig::show_turn_attribution` was intended as the kill switch, but **iter-1645 found it unreachable**: the `From<&BehaviorSettings>` impl filled it with a literal `true` and the key did not exist in `BehaviorSettings` or `operant.example.toml`, so no operator could turn it off. Now threaded as `[agent] show_turn_attribution` (default on), pinned by a test asserting the `From` impl directly -- the TOML parse passes while the impl hardcodes, which is exactly the shape that hid this. `None` means "no attribution attempted", which is a different fact from a span left `Unmeasured`. 5 regression tests + a strengthened emission-site guard; mutation 3 (the emit site hard-coding `None`) passed all 12 runtime tests and was caught only by the source guard. **iter-1631 shipped only 3 of the module's 4 public types wired.** A post-ship audit counting external references per type found `TurnSpan` 14, `SpanDuration` 17, `TurnBreakdown` 4, and **`TurnAttribution` 0** — codex's three-state classifier (`Disabled` / `Incomplete`-naming-the-gap / `Complete`) still had no caller, so the emission carried a raw `TurnBreakdown` and a subscriber could not tell "the model used no tools" from "nobody timed the tools", which is the ambiguity the whole row exists to remove. **iter-1635 closes it**: `OperantAgent::turn_attribution()` returns `Option<TurnAttribution>` and classifies via `TurnAttribution::of()`, `TurnEnd::attribution` carries the classified enum (so `advisor::spawn_advisor` and `recap` both receive it with no signature change — they read fields, not destructure), and the 5 regression tests now assert the classification: a partially captured turn must report `Incomplete` NAMING `[UserWait, Overhead]`, and a turn with no capture must name ALL FOUR. The new source guard `every_public_type_in_this_module_has_a_production_caller` scans the four production seams per public type and additionally requires `TurnAttribution::of` to be called from OUTSIDE the module, so a classifier that is constructed and dropped still fails. **The guard exists because the compiler cannot catch this shape** (`pub` in a `pub mod` emits no `dead_code` for a zero-user type, no gate fails, and `cargo test` is green): that is why RT-209 shipped invisible in the first place, and why iter-1631 left a residue no gate could have caught. ****iter-1642 audit correction: "delivered to every subscriber" was overstated.** A grep for `.attribution` across the workspace returns **ZERO** outside the module itself: `run()` classifies the turn and `TurnEnd` carries the enum into every delivered event, but both subscribers (`advisor.rs`, `recap.rs`) read only `end.session_id`. The chain is live at every layer except the last, and no compiler, clippy, or test can see that gap -- a `pub` field on a `pub` struct in a library emits no `dead_code` warning, so the type-level orphan guard iter-1635 added PASSES on a substring match while the value is still unread. The guard now prints a `KNOWN GAP (RT-209)` notice instead of passing silently (deliberately a notice, not a hard assert: failing the build for a documented intentional state trains the next agent to delete the assertion rather than do the work). Still open as a FEATURE, not a defect: no subscriber reads or renders the breakdown yet -- it is captured and classified; the consumer is the deferred half. The emission is deliberately off the request path, so it cannot touch the frozen-prefix prompt-cache invariant. One iteration's row, deliberately NOT bundled into the audit that found it, because it touches the request path where a careless edit breaks the frozen-prefix prompt-cache invariant. **iter-1655 validation: the orphan returned one level DOWN, at method granularity.** Enumerating every PUBLIC item in the module (not just the four type names the guard checks) found six public methods beyond the constructors, and TWO of them with zero production callers: `TurnBreakdown::is_exclusive()` and `TurnAttribution::render()`. `is_exclusive` appears twice in `stream.rs` and both hits are test assertions; `render` has no caller anywhere. The guard now prints a KNOWN GAP notice per method plus `subscriber_seams_resolve`, which asserts every `SUBSCRIBER_SEAMS` path exists. Three first-draft errors, each caught by mutation: `used_in` counted TEST code as a caller (fixed by `used_in_production`, which cuts the file at its first `#[cfg(test)]`), a bare "render" needle matched 11 times in `run.rs` and 18 in `mod.rs` as parts of unrelated identifiers (needles are now call sites), and `SUBSCRIBER_SEAMS` named `src/agent/advisor.rs` when the real file is `src/advisor.rs` -- an unreadable path counts as no-match, so the typo silently deleted two of six checks. **This is the third variant of the same defect in this module** (zero-caller type, unread field, uncalled method), which says the lesson is not "be more careful": it is that a `pub` item in a `pub mod` in a library crate has NO compiler-visible dead-warning, so every public item needs an explicit production-caller check or it will ship invisible again. iter-1655's draft also lost its uncommitted work to a peer's concurrent push and was reconstructed before committing -- the reason it is committed in the same turn it was edited. **iter-1659 validation: the emission site is guarded, but the LAYER THAT MAKES IT REACHABLE was not, and the ledger's 'the emission is live at every layer' claim was never checked against a real install.** The emission in `run.rs` sits inside `if let Some(ref bus) = self.turn_end_bus`, and `turn_end_bus` is `None` unless a HOST attaches one. `with_turn_end_bus` -- the only public setter -- has ZERO callers. Of the two attaching paths, `attach_advisor` early-returns on `[advisor] enabled = false`, which is the DEFAULT, so it attaches nothing on a stock install; `attach_recap_engine` attaches unconditionally. The verified state: `gateway_runner.rs` and `tui/adapter_types/tui_app.rs` each call it unconditionally BEFORE the enabled-gated advisor, so both real hosts do emit. That is a fact about two files in ANOTHER crate, and no guard pinned it, so any host refactor could have quietly made every span invisible while all 16 attribution tests stayed green. New guard `every_host_attaches_the_turn_end_bus` pins it against the call site in each host. **Its first draft was BLIND**, and mutation proved it: renaming the call to `agent.attach_recap_engine_DISABLED(` left the test green because the bare method name still matched as a substring. The needle is now `agent.attach_recap_engine(` with the receiver and opening paren. That is the FOURTH substring-shaped check this module has shipped (type name in a signature, `render` inside unrelated identifiers, `is_exclusive` in test code, a renamed call), which is the strongest evidence yet that every guard here must use a call-site-shaped needle rather than a name. **iter-1661 -- THE DEFERRED HALF LANDED (the consumer), and the row now closes on the value the operator can see.** `TurnEndBus::log_attribution` renders one `debug!` line per turn at the emission site, `run()` calls it under the `Option`, and `TurnAttribution::render_one_line` prints all four spans with `n/a` for an unmeasured one (never `0ms` -- the RT-199 contract made visible; a new test pins it four ways: total present, `tools=n/a` present, `tools=0ms` absent, all four span names present). Chosen over a TUI panel deliberately: the seam already holds the classified enum AND the guarantee the turn is over, so a line there makes the value observable with no new architecture and no peer-area TUI surface. **What is still open, named not implied:** no SUBSCRIBER reads `end.attribution` off the delivered event -- both existing subscribers (`advisor.rs`, `recap.rs`) still read only `end.session_id`, so the value the event CARRIES is dropped while the seam log consumes the local variable. `TurnBreakdown::is_exclusive()` also has no production caller, and the multi-line `render()` has none (the seam uses `render_one_line`). The guard now ASSERTS the seam consumer exists (mutation-proved: deleting the call in `run.rs` fails `every_public_type_in_this_module_has_a_production_caller` by name) and separately NOTICES the absent subscriber. **A fifth substring-shaped guard was caught in this very iteration:** the seam-consumer assert first used the bare needle `log_attribution(`, which matches the DEFINITION in `turn_end.rs`, so deleting the call left the test green; the needle is now `TurnEndBus::log_attribution(`. A definition is not a caller -- the same lesson as a test assertion or an unrelated identifier fragment, learned for the fifth time in one module. **iter-1650 validation pass (three findings, none a code defect):** (a) the deployed release was one commit STALE for iter-1645's own deliverable: the gateway restarted at 09:06 from a base before `a15662ae` landed, and `strings` on `/home/ishanp/.local/bin/operant` showed `show_turn_attribution` with ZERO hits -- the kill switch was not in the running process at all. A provenance-fresh release was cut from the tip that carries the fix (artifact mtime 10:04:59 vs commit 10:00:14) and deployed; `strings` now finds the key in the binary. (b) the RT-209 row's own prose still read "What stays OPEN: the emission site the plan specified and nobody built" after iter-1631 shipped that emission; corrected to name the consumer. (c) the read-guard's positives were mutation-proved FOR THE FIRST TIME: appending the literal `end.attribution` to a production seam drops the `KNOWN GAP` notice (1 -> 0), so the guard detects a read rather than merely passing on any file content. An earlier probe of mine that reported no effect was itself wrong -- it wrote a comment containing no substring -- recorded here because a guard whose detector is untested is the exact failure this module shipped twice.

| RT-211 | The rewind selector's caption carries a stale cell after a filter close (found 2026-11-02) | **CLOSED iter-1685 (fix + mutation-proven test + golden refresh)** — root cause is a WIDE-GLYPH diff hole, not a missing clear: the caption's marker was `⏪` (U+23EA), and ratatui's `Paragraph` diff writes a wide grapheme at its column while treating the NEXT cell as its continuation WITHOUT rewriting it. Closing the filter shrinks the header from two rows to one, so the caption's row slides up onto the row that held `  filter: ` — whose third character is `i` — and the caption's second space is served from that stale cell. Measured with two frames on one `TestBackend` through `draw_rewind_selector`, then narrowed by a control that swaps only the marker width. Fix: a NARROW marker (`>>`), one cell wide. | RT-242 | The MCP panel's tool filter could not hold an 'r' or an 'e' — typing a search term silently RESTARTED the MCP runtime (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1793** — the MCP panel's letter shortcuts ran in EVERY pane, so the tool list's filter could never hold an 'r' or an 'e': the 'r' arm set `pending_mcp_reconnect` (the runtime is reconnected on the very next frame) and the 'e' arm toggled the error detail, both before the filter arm ever saw the character. MEASURED by driving the real handler: typing **"read"** left the filter holding **"ad"** — the 'r' restarted the MCP runtime and the 'e' expanded the error. Most tool names contain an 'r' or an 'e' ("create", "read", "execute", "search", "server"), so the panel's only way to find a tool was broken for most queries, and a stray letter could drop the operator's MCP servers mid-session. **Fixed**: the shortcuts act on the PANE that owns them — the tool list is a plain text field again (every character filters), 'q'/'a'/'r' act on the Servers pane (where the panel opens) and 'e' on the panes that are not the tool list; Esc still closes from anywhere. The footer now says so, and it FITS the narrow panel (the old line was clipped at 80 columns — "r reconn"). **Pinned** by `the_mcp_tool_filter_holds_every_letter`, mutation-proven (restoring the global arms leaves the filter holding "ad" and fails the assertion by name). The scenario's own note carried two stale claims about `/mcp <args>` (it says the arm "returns false" and calls `/mcp r` "the documented reconnect form" — the arm shells out and returns true, and `operant mcp` has NO `r` subcommand); the note now says what is true. |
| RT-241 | The command palette printed its category header AGAIN AND AGAIN — its rows were in registration order, so the categories interleaved (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1791** — the palette's rows were built in REGISTRATION order, and the renderer prints a category header whenever the category CHANGES (`item.category != last_category`). The registry's order does not group by category, so the categories INTERLEAVED and the same header came back over and over: the corpus's own golden showed "Other" FOUR times in the first twenty rows, and the mutation dump shows **twelve** separate "Other" runs across the 114 rows — i.e. the palette printed ~40 headers for 11 categories, most of them the catch-all. A palette whose headers repeat is a palette whose grouping is invisible. **Fixed**: the rows are sorted by category (a STABLE sort, so the registration order survives inside a category), and the category enum's declaration order is the section order with the catch-all **last**. `tui_category` now returns the enum instead of a display string (it had exactly one caller), so the sort key and the label cannot disagree. **Pinned** by `the_command_palette_groups_its_rows_by_category`, which asserts every category is ONE contiguous run — mutation-proven (removing the sort fails it by name, printing the interleaved sequence it rejected). The corpus golden is re-proved: the palette now reads Model & Provider, Review & History, Diagnostics, … each header once. **RESIDUAL, named not hidden:** the category TABLE is a second catalogue that covers only 54 of the 114 registered commands, so 60 of them (52%) land in the catch-all "Other" — one section now instead of twelve runs, but still the majority. Covering them is a product decision about the category set, not a rendering fix. |
| RT-240 | The corpus's own notes claimed the typeahead "paint[s] zero rows" for two-or-more-character prefixes — the defect does not exist (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1788** — `typeahead-suggestions.scenario.json`'s notes said "OBSERVED while authoring: two-or-more-character prefixes ('/sk', '/he', '/ex') currently paint zero rows while single-character prefixes do — a real inconsistency worth a follow-up, but not this scenario's job." MEASURED 2026-11-06 against the corpus's own pinned environment at both corpus sizes (120x40 and 80x24): the claim is FALSE — `/sk` paints the /skills row, `/he` paints the /help row, `/ex` paints the /exit row. The popup paints its rows for every prefix, one character or more. A note in the corpus's own notes naming a live defect that does not exist is the same shape as a stale claim in AGENTS.md (RT-216) or a doc naming a join section that does not exist (RT-217): the next reader goes hunting in working code, or worse "fixes" it into a regression. **Fixed**: the note now records the measurement and says the claim was false, and the behaviour is PINNED — a new 100x30 variant types a two-character prefix and asserts the matching row is painted (and that a different command's row is NOT), proved able to fail by running it with the wrong expectation ("Screen assertion failed: expected to contain '/skills …'"). |
| RT-239 | The `/help` overlay's command rows were a STALE SECOND COPY of the registry, and they advertised argument forms no command reads (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1786** — iter-1766 fixed four rows in the command TABLE, and the overlay's hand-written "Commands" section kept the old text: it was a second copy of the catalogue, and it had drifted further than the table had. **The argument forms it advertised are not implemented**: `/model <name>`, `/effort <level>`, `/config init`, `/config edit`, `/plan [goal]`, `/improve resume`, `/refactor resume` and `/save [label]` are all ignored by their arms (and `/rename --clear` renames the session to the literal string "--clear"), while the rows promised a model switch, a nine-level effort picker, a config file, a plan card, a resumable loop and a bookmark. The descriptions of the rows that WERE implemented had drifted too: `/reload` promised "Reload to newer binary if available" and reloads settings from disk, `/plan` promised a plan card and toggles a read-only permission mode, `/clear` promised "and start fresh" and only clears the conversation (`/new` starts a fresh session), `/version` promised "build details" and prints one version line, `/config` promised "Show active configuration" and opens the settings screen, `/resume` promised a picker and opens the session hub, `/login` promised "Interactive or direct login" and runs the provider setup wizard. And the "More commands" sweep used the row set that INCLUDES the remote-only commands, so a LOCAL session's `/help` listed `/continue` and `/resumeall` — whose answer here is "registered but not wired in operant yet", while the typeahead (which filters the same rows out) did not offer them. **Fixed**: the overlay's command rows read their description from the registry (the ONE catalogue), so a hand-written copy cannot drift again; the argument forms no command reads are gone, and the ones that exist (`/help <text>`, `/memory <cmd>`, `/rename <name>`) are listed; four registry descriptions that were themselves wrong (`/plan`, `/config`, `/resume`, `/login`) now say what the arms do; and a local `/help` lists only the commands a local session can run, with the remote-only rows reserved for a bridge session. **Pinned** by three render guards over the real overlay (`every_local_command_shows_its_registry_description_in_the_overlay`, `a_local_help_overlay_does_not_list_the_remote_only_commands`, `the_overlay_no_longer_advertises_argument_forms_the_commands_ignore`), all mutation-proven. |
| RT-234 | The `/help` overlay's filter was DEAD in the Commands view, and `/help <command>` dropped its argument — the row and the footer both promised a feature that did nothing (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1785** — `HelpOverlay::filter` is documented as "only commands matching this substring are shown", and only the `/keys` and `/hotkeys` views ever read it: `draw_help_overlay` (the Commands view) ignored it entirely, so every keystroke an operator typed in `/help` was swallowed by a filter no render consulted — the overlay looked frozen and the characters never reached the composer either. The advertised `/help <command>` form was worse: the arm toggled the overlay whatever it was given, so `/help model` opened exactly the same unfiltered overlay `/help` does, while the overlay's own row ("Show details for one command") and its footer ("/help <cmd> for details") both promised the argument did something. **Fixed**: the Commands view filters its rows the same way the Keys view does (a row matches when any of its spans carries the term, so the command name AND its description are searchable), the filter is shown in the title, a filter that matches nothing says so instead of showing an empty overlay, and `/help <command>` opens the overlay filtered on the term. **Pinned** by `help_with_an_argument_opens_the_overlay_filtered_on_it` (the dispatch half) plus the corpus's new `help-overlay.100x30` variant, which renders the filtered frame and asserts the `/model` row is on screen and `/changelog` is not. |
| RT-233 | `/memory` was a registered command that could only print a usage dump — the `/memory on|off` form /help advertised does not exist (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1781** — the arm passed the operator's argument straight through to `operant memory`, and `operant memory` REQUIRES a subcommand (clap). So a bare `/memory` ran `operant memory` and printed the usage dump, and the form the /help overlay advertised (`/memory on`, `/memory off`) ran `operant memory on` → "error: unrecognized subcommand 'on'" — that toggle does not exist in `operant memory` at all. The registry's own description ("Memory-wire status (operant memory)") named a status view the arm could not produce. **Fixed**: a bare `/memory` is now the status view (`operant memory stats`), and a subcommand runs for real (list | get | search | store | delete | stats | import | export | clear). A free-text tail (a memory, a query, a path) stays ONE argv element so `operant memory search my query` actually reaches the query; flags (`--limit 5`, `--confirm`) stay split. Pinned by `memory_runs_a_real_subcommand_instead_of_printing_the_usage_dump`, mutation-proved in both directions (restoring the pass-through arm fails on the bare case; splitting the free-text tail fails on the query case). |
| RT-232 | A THIRD answer to "how big is the context window" — the flat 128000 stub the warning path fell back to (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1780** — `context_window_for_model` returned a hardcoded 128000 for every model, and it was still the token-warning path's fallback whenever the footer's cell was 0 (before the first refresh). Its own doc claimed it "is still used by refresh_context_window_size in app.rs" — false since iter-1769, which is exactly why it survived: a helper whose doc names its last reader. With the footer on the agent's window and the gateway on the agent's window, the stub was a third answer to the same question, and the warning that decides whether auto-compact runs could divide by a number neither surface shows. **Deleted**, with the warning's pre-refresh fallback now the CONFIGURED value (the same source the refresh reads, and what the agent budgets against when no limit has been learned). |
| RT-231 | The TUI's footer and the gateway's /context quoted two different context windows again (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1779** — the iter-1207 two-denominator defect, back. iter-1769 changed the TUI's `refresh_context_window_size` to read the configured `[agent] context_window` (128k) and added `OperantAgent::context_window()` — public, with the doc "**Public because CLI and TUI surfaces must report the same denominator the agent uses**" — but left the gateway's `/context` on its own resolver (the models.dev cache with the per-provider fallbacks: anthropic → 200k). So the TUI's footer said `8/128k` while `/context` said `0 / 200.0k`: the same session's two surfaces disagreeing about how full the context was, and both about a number the CORE does not budget against (the core budgets against the agent's window — the configured one, lowered by a limit a prior overflow taught us). The gateway's own resolver is now gone, the gateway takes `agent.context_window()`, and the TUI's footer takes the agent's value whenever the agent exists. |
| RT-229 | The simulator had no way to say "this run is EXPECTED to log errors" (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1778** — `operant tui debug simulate` fails any run whose event log contains an error, with no opt-out. So a scenario that DELIBERATELY drives a turn into a provider failure could never be gated — and it stopped being gable the moment iter-1774 made a failed turn a real event on the bus (the right change: "the failure must be an event on the bus, not only a stored string"). The corpus's `failed-turn-no-duplicate-prompt` scenario went red for that reason. **Fixed in the tool**: `--expect-errors` tolerates the errors (they are still printed) and REQUIRES at least one, so a scenario that stopped simulating its failure cannot quietly pass. The scenario opts in through the schema's existing `flags` field. |
| RT-230 | Unit tests rewrote the operator's real settings.json (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1778** — three settings tests call `apply_and_save`, which persists through `Settings::save_sync` to `operant_home()/settings.json` — the OPERATOR'S FILE. Every suite run rewrote their configuration, and the next run read back whatever the last one wrote. The coupling is not theoretical: `every_settings_entry_has_an_applier` builds its default screen from the ambient settings, and a test that had enabled file injection made the "default" screen offer the conditional rows too — so the guard began failing for a reason that had nothing to do with the guard (a chase that cost a round's worth of time). **Fixed**: a `with_sandbox_home` helper (the crate-wide `test_env_lock` + a `HERMES_HOME` sandbox, the same pattern `app/tests.rs` uses for the history file) wraps every test that saves, and the guard builds both screens with their conditional flag set explicitly rather than from the ambient file. Proved by watching the write land in the sandbox home instead of the operator's. |
| RT-228 | The catalogue advertised "Alt+V — Toggle Vim mode" while the repo had PINNED that Alt+V must never become a vim toggle (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1775** — the catalogue's Prompt context carried a row "Alt+v — Toggle Vim mode" for years, while the repo's own `test_alt_v_does_not_toggle_vim_mode` pinned the opposite: Alt+V must never silently become a vim toggle (the voice hold-to-talk chord was purged at iter-668 and deliberately left unbound), and vim is reached through the `/vim` command. Nothing compared the catalogue against the dispatch, so the two disagreed for years — the same hole that let iter-1758's Ctrl+Q and iter-1770's wrong-context rows survive. **The catalogue was the part that was wrong** (the dispatch and the pinned test agreed), so the row is GONE rather than the chord wired: the registry's own rule for a chord with no action applies — leave it uncatalogued rather than re-bind it. A guard (`alt_v_stays_uncatalogued`) keeps it gone, and the Prompt context's 21 rows — the composer's own chords, previously unpinned by any test — are now pinned to their dispatch arms. |
| RT-239 | `operant sessions list` PANICKED on the operator's own session title (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1791** — the list table truncated a title with a BYTE slice (`&title[..25]`), and a byte slice panics when the cut lands inside a multi-byte character. The operator's session title carries an em-dash, so the command printed "end byte index 25 is not a char boundary" and DIED — in the one command an operator runs to SEE their sessions. Found by running the deployed binary against the live database, not by reading the code. The same byte-slicing shape sat in four other display paths (the checkpoint reason, the masked API key, the TUI's session id, the stats dialog's model id); all five are char-safe now, and the sessions table reuses the file's own `truncate_str` helper (which was already char-safe — the table simply did not use it). Pinned by `cmd_sessions::tests::a_title_with_a_multi_byte_character_is_truncated_without_panicking`. |
| RT-238 | The session distillation failed on every model answer that wrapped its facts in a sentence — so the self-improvement path stored nothing (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1787** — the distillation asks the model for a JSON array of durable facts and parses the reply with `serde_json::from_str`. The model often wraps that array in prose ("Here are the facts: [...]") or in a fence the stripper did not catch, and the parse then failed on the FIRST character ("expected value at line 1 column 1") — MEASURED on the operator's live gateway log: **27 distillations failed that way**, each one a session whose facts were dropped instead of retained. The distillation is the harness's own self-improvement path (the facts are what a later session recalls), so a parser that only accepts a bare array silently disables it. **Fixed**: the payload is the ARRAY — the parser now takes the first '[' that opens it and the last ']', trying a leading '[' first and then the next candidates, so prose and a trailing sentence no longer lose the facts. Pinned by two new unit tests (`parses_an_array_wrapped_in_prose`, `parses_an_array_inside_a_fence_followed_by_prose`) in `distillation.rs`. The failure message now names the response length instead of a serde position, because the position was the part that told the operator nothing. |
| RT-237 | A RESUMED session lost its ENTIRE tool history — the model saw a conversation with no tools in it (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1787** — a tool row persisted WITHOUT its `tool_call_id` cannot be paired with the assistant turn that requested it, and the rehydration's orphan repair DROPS such a row (`drop_orphaned_tool_messages`: "a tool message with no id at all can never be matched, so it is dropped too") — and then strips the calls of the assistant turns that asked for them, so the turn loses BOTH halves. The writer has carried the id since iter-1769, but every row written BEFORE that has none, and nothing repaired them: MEASURED on the operator's live database, 407 of the 437 tool rows in `sess_56bae289…` had no id (and ~25 000 rows across the other live sessions), and that turn's own repair log counted **818 dropped halves** — the whole tool history, gone on every resumed turn. The operator's report ("the resumed sessions do not have their entire context") is this row. **Fixed**: the rehydration recovers the missing ids from the transcript's ORDER — an assistant turn's tool results follow it, one per call, in the order the calls were made — and a row that already has an id keeps it and claims its call, so a turn written partly before the fix and partly after it pairs correctly. MEASURED on the live data with the shipped algorithm: 8 741 + 7 790 + 5 609 + 1 262 + 875 + 803 tool rows recovered across six live sessions, and **0** rows ended up paired with a call no assistant turn made. The tool NAME is recovered the same way, so the restored transcript names the tool too. Pinned by `crates/operant-core/tests/session_tool_pairing.rs` (an id-less result is paired again; a mixed turn keeps the id it has and pairs the rest by order). |
| RT-234 | An early turn ended with NOTHING: the operator got an empty answer and a notice that blamed the wrong cause (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1783** — a turn that runs out of room ends with a TOOLLESS wrap-up. When that wrap-up came back empty or degenerate the turn stopped with an empty answer, and the TUI's notice said "the wrap-up ran out of room mid-summary" — the live incident (2026-11-05 20:25) was the OTHER failure: the wall clock stopped the turn, the wrap-up emitted a malformed tool call ("Failed to parse tool_call content, content_len: 555"), and the S1 quality gate threw the 13-character result away ("Grace summary rejected by the quality gate — nothing persisted"). The operator was told the model ran out of room when the model had answered and the answer was garbage, and the agentic-core had NO handling for it: the turn died there. **Fixed**: the core now issues a bounded synthetic continuation — the auto-poke, ported from jcode's mechanism (`crates/jcode-todo-policy/src/lib.rs` `build_auto_poke_message`, `crates/jcode-tui/src/tui/app/commands_auto_poke_errors.rs` `is_non_retryable_auto_poke_error`) — which gives the turn one more pass WITH its tools, bypassing the iteration budget and the wall clock that just stopped it. Bounded three ways: at most 2 pokes per turn, each granting 3 iterations past the limit; only when there is work to continue (an open todo list, or a tool call that SUCCEEDED — a turn whose every tool failed is a stuck model, and poking it would only repeat the failing calls); and never after a non-retryable provider error. The "Turn ended early" notice now names the cause that happened: cut off by the output limit is "out of room", rejected by the quality gate is "no usable summary". Pinned by `crates/operant-core/tests/auto_poke.rs`. |
| RT-235 | The session-rehydration warning fired on EVERY load and reported the KEPT count as the dropped one (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1783** — `SessionStore::load_from_db` computed `dropped = total - start`, and `start` is already `total - kept`, so the two cancelled and the log reported the KEPT count as the dropped one: the live gateway log carried "rows_total: 643, rows_kept: 643, rows_dropped: 643" on every single load — every resumed session was announced as starting mid-session, whether it did or not (a 643-row transcript that lost NOTHING). The warning is the operator's only record that a long transcript was truncated, so a warning that always fires and always lies is worse than no warning: it trains the reader to ignore the one line that would have mattered. **Fixed**: the count is the rows actually dropped, and the warning fires only when rows were dropped. Pinned by `crates/operant-core/tests/session_rehydration_log.rs` (the count, and the absence of the false warning for a session that fits). |
| RT-236 | The token estimate charged context the provider does not charge — the agent compacted requests that were nowhere near the cap (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1783** — `estimate_message_tokens` counted the assistant's reasoning. The reasoning is not context: the Anthropic adapter drops it (`build_assistant_content` emits only text and tool_use blocks) and the OpenAI adapter sends it as `reasoning_content`, which the provider does not bill against the window. MEASURED against the live `large-stack` endpoint on 2026-11-06: 18 000 characters of `reasoning_content` added **15** prompt tokens to the next request (4 027 total, 3 904 of them cached). The live session carried 428 693 bytes of reasoning — ~107 000 phantom tokens on every request — so the agent believed it was at 418 711 tokens when the provider was serving ~200 000, and the preflight ladder compacted EVERY turn ("Compacted context: 418711 → 341122 tokens, 644 → 645 messages") on a 1 M window whose soft cap is 350 k. The RT-83 row's premise ("the reasoning IS serialised back to the provider") was true of the WIRE but not of the provider's BILLING, and the estimate followed the wire. **Fixed**: the estimator charges what the provider charges. The soft cap (350 k) and the hard cap (400 k) now mean what the operator configured. |
| RT-227 | `/output-style verbose` cycled the style instead of setting it (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1773** — the command's arm cycled whatever the argument was, so `/output-style verbose` moved the style to **stream**: the operator's level silently became the NEXT one — the same class of silent-argument-substitution the count commands had (RT-226). An unknown level ("/output-style loud") was accepted the same way, with no word about it. **Fixed**: a named level is now SET, an unknown one is refused by name (""loud" is not an output style — use auto | stream | verbose."), and no argument still cycles. The registry's descriptions for `/output-style` and its `/verbose` alias now say so, because a description that says "Cycle" while the command also takes a level is the next version of the same lie. |
| RT-226 | A count argument the operator typed was silently turned into a different count — and /copy 0 blamed an empty transcript (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1772** — the commands that take a count (`/copy [N]`, `/undo [N]`) parsed it with `unwrap_or(default)`, so `"abc"`, `"-3"` and an overflowing number all became **1**: `/copy abc` copied one message and never mentioned the argument it could not read, and `/undo abc` silently undid ONE TURN the operator never named. `/undo 0` was worse — it was clamped UP to 1, rewinding a message the operator had asked not to rewind. And `/copy 0` (which the corpus's own test pins as a real answer: copy nothing) fell through to the empty-transcript notice, so a transcript with six messages in it was reported as "No messages to copy — the transcript is empty." — a false statement sent to an operator who then hunts for a transcript that is right there. **Fixed**: a count is either a count or an error (`parse_last_n` now returns `Result` and the arms name the argument they could not read), `/undo 0` says it needs at least one turn and undoes nothing, and `/copy 0` says the count was 0 — the empty-transcript notice now fires only for an empty transcript. |
| RT-225 | The vim modes' catalogue rows were in the WRONG context, and Ctrl+C in a vim mode wiped the composer's text (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1770** — the catalogue's vim contexts were audited against the vim dispatch (`prompt_input/vim*.rs`) with the same (context, chord) matrix the chord catalogue uses. Two defects: (1) `n` and `N` (repeat the last search forward/backward) were catalogued under **VimSearch**, but the dispatch accepts them in **Normal** mode — in the search line they are ordinary characters and type an "n"/"N" into the pattern, so `/keys` told the operator that pressing `n` in the search line finds the next match. The rows moved to VimNormal. (2) The catalogue's VimCommand and VimSearch rows have always said "Ctrl+c — Exit to Normal mode", but the app's Ctrl+C arm had no vim-mode guard: it CLEARED the composer's text and started the quit confirmation. An operator who pressed Ctrl+C to abort a half-typed vim command lost their whole prompt and was asked whether they wanted to quit the app. The dispatch now leaves the mode (as the catalogue promises, and as vim does) without touching the prompt; the visual contexts' rows were added, since the same path serves them. |
| RT-224 | The keybinding catalogue's PROMPT-context rows were a stale second copy — /keys printed one chord as two different features (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1768** — the catalogue keeps a second row for a chord in the Prompt context, and those rows had drifted from the dispatch. Measured against `app/key_handling.rs`: **Ctrl+T** was catalogued as "Copy mode (drag-select with the keyboard)" when the copy mode moved to Alt+Y at plan 08 and Ctrl+T became the thinking toggle (the Global row already said so — /keys printed both); **Alt+Y** was catalogued as "Yank pop", which no arm implements (Ctrl+Y is the kill-ring yank); **Alt+Up/Alt+Down** were catalogued as "scroll transcript up/down a page" when they scroll 20 rows; **Ctrl+Up/Ctrl+Down** as "scroll transcript up/down" when they scroll 3. Nine rows corrected to what their Global twin says (the context column already says where each applies). **The guard's hole is closed**: `every_advertised_binding_dispatches` used to require that AT LEAST ONE Global/Prompt row for a chord carried the pinned description — which a stale second copy cannot fail. It now requires EVERY such row to carry it, so one chord means one thing in every context. Restoring the stale Ctrl+T Prompt row fails it by name and context. |
| RT-223 | Two vendored messages pointed at commands operant does not have — "/toolsets" and "/reset" (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1767** — the same rebrand class as the tips strip's stale chords: the strings were renamed jcode → operant while the COMMANDS they name stayed jcode's. The `/tools` handler's reply said "Use /toolsets for the full list" — there is no `/toolsets` (not in the TUI's table, not in the handler registry), so the MODEL that read the reply tried a command that does not exist and asked again, and the MCP panel's tool pane is not the list either (it holds the MCP servers' tools, not the agent's own). The OpenAI usage hint ended "/reset usage limits openai" — there is no `/reset`, and the core has no banked-reset action either (the credits are display-only data), so the hint promised an action the product does not have. Both corrected, and the class is now guarded: `every_command_a_user_facing_string_points_at_exists` scans the TUI's own strings for command references in prose and checks each against the command table AND the handler registry. The scan is narrow on purpose — a slash plus a lowercase word sitting after a space/bullet/dash/bracket, and not followed by "/" (a path) — which is why it finds exactly one decision entry (`/tmp`) instead of eighty false positives. Reintroducing `/toolsets` fails it naming the file and line. |
| RT-222 | Four of the /help overlay's 111 command DESCRIPTIONS no longer say what the commands do (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1766** — the command table's descriptions are what the operator reads BEFORE pressing the key, and unlike the chord catalogue (guarded since plan 10 by `every_advertised_binding_dispatches`) the command table had NO guard. A sweep of all 111 rows against their dispatch arms found four stale: **/branch** promised "the fork tree of this session's branches", but the fork-tree overlay was replaced by the session hub on the branch filter (iter-1467) — the arm opens the hub; **/logout** promised "Log out of a provider" when the TUI holds no credential material and the arm only reports where the keys live (`~/.operant/.env`) and routes to /login; **/save** promised "Bookmark session for easy access" and opens the EXPORT dialog — a different feature entirely; **/effort** listed six wire values ("off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh") when the picker has only ever offered four rows (low | normal | high | max). All four corrected, and a guard now pins them: `the_help_overlay_descriptions_match_what_the_arms_do` checks the registry STRINGS and the arms' BEHAVIOUR (the hub opens on the branch filter, /save opens the export dialog, /logout reports the key location, /effort opens the picker), so neither side can drift without failing. Restoring the old /save description fails it by name. |
| RT-221 | The scroll-bookmark notice told the operator to press Ctrl+G to return — Ctrl+G is the EXTERNAL EDITOR (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1763** — the notice "Bookmark on at row {at} — Ctrl+G returns here." named the chord the bookmark used BEFORE it moved to Alt+G (iter-1267). Pressing it as the notice instructed opened the operator's external editor instead of returning them to the row they had just bookmarked — a scroll position lost to a wrong chord in the one message that tells the operator how to use the feature. Found by the same sweep as RT-220: every user-facing string that names a chord checked against the keybinding catalogue. **Fixed and pinned**: the notice names `Alt+G`, the function's doc comment (which carried the same stale chord) is corrected, and a test asserts the notice names Alt+G and does NOT name Ctrl+G — proved RED by restoring the wrong chord. |
| RT-220 | The tips strip advertised THREE chords that no longer did what the tips said (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1762** — the tips widget is the one surface the operator reads on a loop (it rotates every 15 s), so a chord that no longer does what the tip says sends the operator to the wrong feature on purpose. Measured against the keybinding catalogue: (1) "**Ctrl+G or Alt+G toggles a scroll bookmark**" — Ctrl+G is the EXTERNAL EDITOR (the bookmark moved to Alt+G at iter-1267); pressing it opened the operator's editor instead of the bookmark. (2) "**Ctrl+T enters drag-select copy mode**" — Ctrl+T toggles the THINKING DISPLAY (copy mode moved from Ctrl+T to Alt+Y at plan 08). (3) "**PageUp / PageDown scroll 10 lines**" — the live step is one PAGE (the transcript viewport's height minus two rows of overlap); 10 is only the fallback for a headless app that has published no frame. All three are now corrected, and the module's comment claiming every tip was "verified against the keybinding registry / dispatch arms" was itself false. **A guard now closes the loop**: `every_chord_a_tip_names_agrees_with_the_catalogue` pins each tip's prose to a table row and each row's claim to the CATALOGUE's own description for that chord, and it refuses any chord a tip names that the table does not pin. Both old tips are caught: restoring the Ctrl+G tip fails with "the tip names Ctrl+G, which this test does not pin", and restoring the Ctrl+T tip fails with "no tip contains ... — the claim this test pins is gone". |
| RT-219 | The settings screen offered "File injection max size", the operator edited it, and the save DROPPED it — and the guard that exists for exactly this class never saw the row (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1760** — RT-171's defect class, one row over: `all_entries` offers 19 editable settings and `apply_and_save` had **no case** for `fileInjectionMaxSize`, so the operator's edit rendered, landed in `pending_changes`, and was silently discarded while the whole settings.json was rewritten from the snapshot. **Why no gate caught it: the row is only OFFERED when file injection is enabled** (`all_entries` pushes the three file-injection rows under `if screen.file_injection_enabled`), and the guard `every_settings_entry_has_an_applier` derived its key list from the DEFAULT screen — where those rows are not offered at all. The guard passed because it was checking 16 rows, not 19. **Fixed in two places**: `apply_and_save` now applies the value (`settings.config.file_injection_max_size`, `usize`, same shape as its `fileAutocompleteLimit` sibling), and the guard checks BOTH screens — the default one and one with file injection enabled — and ASSERTS that the second offers MORE rows, so the conditional coverage cannot quietly disappear again. A behavioural test walks the operator's real path (turn injection on, then edit the max size) and was proved RED before the fix ("left: 0, right: 2048"). Removing the new applier arm fails BOTH tests. |
| RT-218 | The keybindings catalogue advertised Ctrl+Q as "Quit application" and NOTHING dispatched it (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1758** — the Global table has listed `Ctrl+Q → Cancel → "Quit application"` since it was written, and no arm in `app/key_handling.rs` handled a Ctrl+Q at all: the operator pressed the chord the help screen promised and nothing happened. The source-level keybindings guard could not see it, because it asks only whether the key TOKEN appears somewhere in the dispatch file — and `KeyCode::Char('c')` does. **The mechanism had a second half.** The exit-confirmation state machine is split: the arms call `handle_exit_key_confirmation` (they start and complete the two-press sequence) and a reset at the END of `handle_key_event` wipes the sequence for every key outside `{Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D}`. So even with an arm, a chord missing from that list has its own state cleared between the two presses — the sequence can never complete, and the chord looks like it does nothing. **Fixed**: Ctrl+Q now arms the same two-press confirmation (and, unlike Ctrl+C, does NOT clear the composer — a chord pressed by accident must not destroy a typed prompt before the exit is confirmed), the reset list names every chord the confirmation accepts, and the confirmation message names the chord it is asking about. **Two tests**: `ctrl_q_asks_for_confirmation_and_then_exits` is BEHAVIOURAL (the first press asks, the second exits) — proved RED before the fix — and `every_exit_chord_survives_the_key_handlers_reset` pins the INVARIANT that every chord a confirmation arm accepts is named in the reset list, so the next chord cannot repeat this. Dropping `'q'` from the reset list fails BOTH tests. **Live evidence, with its limit stated**: in a real pty the first Ctrl+Q shows "Press Ctrl+Q again to exit" (so the chord reaches the handler in a terminal), but the second press does not terminate the app in this sandbox's tmux — and the SHIPPED Ctrl+C does not terminate there either (it shows no notice at all), so the two-press termination is verified at the unit level and the live non-termination is a pre-existing behaviour of the shipped chord in this environment, not a regression from this change. |
| RT-217 | The TUI's live-verification tool could not run its own documented recipe, and silently produced a capture with its determinism controls lost (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1753** — `scripts/tui-capture.sh` had THREE defects, all found by RUNNING it. (1) **A failed `mktemp` became the filesystem root.** The script runs `set -uo pipefail` WITHOUT `-e`, so an empty `PIN_HOME` turned every path into `/operant.toml` and `/.operant`: the config write failed, the child TUI ran with NO pinned config and a broken HOME, and the tool still printed "wrote ... capture" and exited 0 — a capture that silently lost every determinism control the file promises. It now fails loud (exit 2) with the TMPDIR that failed. (2) **The wait was checked where it could never succeed.** `--wait-text` polled BEFORE the keys were typed, so the file's own example — `--keys '/help' --wait-text 'Commands'` — timed out every time: the overlay's text can only appear AFTER the command that opens it. The pre-key wait is now the quiescence strategy and the text wait runs after the submit. (3) **The doc's needles named a section that does not exist.** `docs/library/tui-debugging.md` used `Shortcuts` in three examples (two headless, one live); the help overlay's sections are `Commands`, `Session` and `Memory & Swarm`, pinned by `baselines/help-overlay.txt`, so the live recipe waited for text that never arrives — and its headless twin added a second trap: with no credential pin the first-run "Connect a provider" dialog is MODAL and swallows the typed `/help`, so `overlays.help_overlay == false` and the gate is red for a perfectly good overlay. All needles are `Commands`, the pin is in the example, and both the live recipe and the headless command now pass verbatim as documented. |
| RT-216 | AGENTS.md — the single source of truth — claimed a TUI "workspace view" with Conversation/Reasoning/Activity panes and a `Behavior` management panel that do not exist, and the TUI module count was stale (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1752** — the claim named three surfaces this TUI has never had: there is no workspace view (`grep` for `workspace_view`/`WorkspaceView` across the tree returns nothing), no Conversation/Reasoning/Activity panes, and no Behavior panel. `BehaviorSettings` is CONFIG — the `[agent]` table in `operant.toml`, edited with `operant config set` or by hand — and `/config` in the TUI opens the VISUAL settings screen. The bullet now states what the TUI actually has (MCP, Skills, Plugins, Journey, the session hub, the agents menu) and names the guard `tui::app::tests::behaviour_config_is_not_a_panel`, which pins both halves: no registered command is named `/behavior`/`/behaviour`, and no dispatch arm opens one (a HIDDEN panel would be worse than a missing command, because nothing would advertise it). The Architecture Overview's module count was stale too — "64 TUI modules (303 .rs files)" against the code's 66 modules and 328 files — and `scripts/check-doc-claims.sh` was reporting that drift while exiting 0. Both numbers are corrected and the gate now prints "all AGENTS.md code-surface claims match the code". |
| RT-218 | The TUI's scroll-back counters were painted OVER the transcript they were counting, so a reader in history saw corrupted words (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1754** — the ↓ counter at the render area's last row and the ↑ counter at its first row landed INSIDE `content_area` whenever no top band is reserved, and since the counters paint after the transcript Paragraph they replaced that line's tail. Measured in the corpus: `scroll-pageup-moves-viewport` row 24 rendered `L039 scroll test↓40ne` (the " li" of "scroll test line" eaten by `↓40`) and `scroll-pageup-third-press` row 18 rendered `L032 s↓51ll`; a corpus-wide sweep for a symbol embedded between two alphanumerics found exactly those two. `chat_native_scrollbar()` returns `false` unconditionally so the counters are the live path. The geometry is a byte-identical port of upstream jcode (inherited defect, not a regression). Fixed: each counter paints only into a row's TRAILING WHITESPACE and only where it fits — ↓ searches up from the last row, ↑ searches down from the first; a row with no room is skipped, never truncated. No row reserved, so `max_scroll`/`visible_height`/the resize anchor are unchanged. Mutation-proven in both directions (M1 repaints over text → arm 1 fails with the corruption; M2 suppresses the counter → arm 2 fails), and the first test draft passed under M1 because its fixture's last row was blank — the fixture is now one long message whose wrapped lines fill the viewport. |
| RT-215 | The corpus could not pin the scroll ladder's third rung — the harness had no way to let a frame settle — and the corpus registry described a DELETED MCP-approval dialog as a live product gap (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1751** — two defects in the TUI's own verification story. (1) **The harness had no idle-frame token.** `scroll-pageup-third-press` had carried `deterministic: false` since the corpus repair because its landing line moved with the machine's load: the keys arrived before the mock transcript landed, and the run loop paints BEFORE it applies an event, so `--dump-screen` showed the frame before the last key. The scenario's own notes named the unblock ("a `<wait:ms>` token in cmd_tui_debug.rs's parse_key_sequence"); it is now `<wait:N>` — N IDLE FRAMES, not milliseconds, because a frame count is deterministic by construction while a duration would put the verdict back on the machine's load. The scenario is RE-GATED: `deterministic` and the nondeterminism block are gone, it carries its landing assert again (`contains:L001`, `not-contains:L199`) and its goldens are committed. The ladder it now pins, measured: 0 presses → L145, 1 → L085, 2 → L026, 3 → L001 (the ceiling), 4-6 → L001 (clamped). Mutation-proven: reverting the scroll direction (`saturating_sub` → `saturating_add` in `scroll_up_rows`, the defect class that parked the reader at the tail) fails it with "expected to contain 'L001'", and the base scenario fails with its own "expected to contain 'L020'". (2) **The registry described a deleted surface as a live product gap.** `excluded.json`, `_validate.py`'s SURFACES ledger and `schema.json` all still pointed at `dialogs/mcp_approval.rs::render_mcp_approval_dialog` — a file DELETED at iter-978 — and the reason text claimed "the dialog is fully built — render, key handling, Z-order branch in render_app, dialog_priority entry, overlay_flags entry" for a dialog that no longer exists, pointing the next agent at a call site for a deleted surface. The registry's own rule settles it ("a deleted surface has no render target to park"), so the entries are removed, as `session-browser` and `session-branching` were. The corpus validator's error count went 3 → 2, and the two that remain belong to a peer's untracked scenario, not to this tree. |
| RT-214 | The TUI's command sweep reported 98 BROKEN commands when the simulator could not start at all (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1748** — `command_sweep.py` read ANY non-zero exit as "this command fell through to the model", so a simulator that could not START (no writable HOME, a missing shared library, a crash before the first frame) was reported as 98 broken commands. Measured in a sandbox whose HOME was read-only: `consumed: 0/98`, all 98 under "BROKEN". The sweep now separates CONSUMED / FELL THROUGH / SIMULATOR ERROR (the last one reports the behaviour as UNKNOWN, and still exits non-zero — a gate that cannot verify must not pass), runs HERMETIC (a fresh HOME + HERMES_HOME per sweep, plus the corpus's colour-depth and PATH pins), and has its own regression test (`scripts/tests/command_sweep_test.sh`, wired into `scripts/self-test.sh`) which drives two fake simulators — one that cannot start, one that reports the assertion failure — and asserts each lands in its own class. |
| RT-213 | The TUI crate's own lint gate was RED at tip — 24 diagnostics, including a duplicated `#[test]` that registered a test TWICE (found 2026-11-05) | **CLOSED iter-1747** — `cargo clippy -p operant-cli --all-targets --no-deps -- -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D warnings` now reports ZERO. It reported 24 before. Two items were real defects, not lint noise: (1) a stray `#[test]` sat BEFORE the doc comment in `tui/app/tests.rs` and `tui/rewind_marks.rs`, so the item carried the attribute twice (`duplicate_macro_attributes`) and the harness registered the test TWICE — the suite count drops by exactly one after the strays are removed; (2) `tui/app/key_handling.rs` confirmed an archive with `.take().unwrap()` — the only `unwrap_used` violation in the crate — and now takes the pending id through a `match` that cannot panic. The rest is mechanical (let-chains, `strip_prefix`, struct-init form, a redundant closure) plus honest dead-code handling: the RT-145 restore-path helpers and the trait accessors whose consumers were retired carry `#[expect(dead_code, reason = ...)]` naming that consumer, and `session_hub/tests.rs`'s `row_index` — an orphan of the iter-1733 rewrite — was deleted. |
| RT-199 | Codex portability contrast (iter-1505) | **CLOSED iter-1505** — every `ObserverEvent::ToolCall` carried a hardcoded `Duration::from_millis(0)`, so `ConsoleObserver`'s `duration_ms` was structurally always `0` while the real timings were measured at all three `execute_tools` branches and discarded one hop before the observer. Guard: `crates/operant-core/tests/tool_call_duration_is_real.rs`; `TurnEndBus::tool_durations_ms` could not be reused because it is a name-less `Vec<u64>` in completion order |
| RT-246 | The config template advertised a plugin MANIFEST's fields as CONFIG keys — and the loader rejects both, so following the example breaks the operator's whole config (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1798** — `operant.example.toml`'s `[plugins]` block documented a plugin's `manifest.toml` with live TOML assignments (`requires = ["other-plugin"]`, `provides = ["memory.backend"]`). Those are the MANIFEST's fields, not `operant.toml` keys, and every settings struct uses `deny_unknown_fields` — so an operator who uncommented the example got "unknown field `requires`" and the WHOLE file stopped loading. The template's own gate caught it and was RED at HEAD: `crates/operant-core/tests/example_template_loads.rs::every_commented_example_in_the_template_names_a_field_the_loader_accepts` named lines 568 and 572. The schema already had ONE owner (`docs/library/plugins.md`, lines 22-23 and 55-64); the template was a second copy. **Fixed**: the template points at that owner instead of repeating the schema, and the gate is green again (4/4) |
| RT-247 | A failing aft command reported "unknown error" and threw away the child's own diagnostics — the bridge had already captured them (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1799** — `AftBridge::send_request_once` built its error from the response's `message`/`error` field and fell back to the literal "unknown error" when the response carried neither. The child's stderr was NOT lost: the bridge drains stderr into a 64-line ring for exactly this purpose (plan 07.1) — but the error path never read it, so `aft_inspect` and its siblings answered a failing call with a dead end that named no cause. **Fixed**: a failure with no usable message now reports the child's most recent stderr lines (bounded: the last 5 non-empty lines, joined), and a literal "unknown error" message keeps its name and gains the diagnostics in parentheses. Pinned by `aft_bridge::tests::a_failing_command_without_a_message_reports_the_childs_stderr`, mutation-proved (restoring the old fallback fails it with "aft inspect: [E_NO_INDEX] unknown error" — the exact symptom the row names) |
| RT-248 | The self-extension tools could never run — `harness_mount` / `harness_unmount` refused every call, and the refusal told the operator to approve the tool in the allowlist they had ALREADY approved it in (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1799** — the two tools gate on `ToolContext::metadata["approval"] == "true"`, and NOTHING ever set that flag: the tools are not permission-gated (so they are never prompted for) and the agent's tool context carried only `session_id` / `unattended`. The operator's `command_allowlist` DID reach the agent's persistent allowlist (`agent_config()` → `AgentConfig::approval_allowlist` → `approval_allowlist_from_config`), but the approval stopped there — it was never handed to the tool. So the model could call `harness_mount` and always got "harness_mount requires the host's approval policy to have approved this tool for the current session. Ask the user to approve `harness_mount` (e.g. via the persistent or session allowlist), then retry." — an instruction to do the thing the operator had already done. **Fixed**: the agent's tool context now carries `approval=true` for a tool its allowlist covers (`OperantAgent::tool_context`, `agent/stream.rs`), so the documented route works. Pinned by `agent::tests::an_allowlisted_tool_tells_itself_that_it_was_approved`, mutation-proved (dropping the flag fails it by name) |
| RT-249 | A delegation that produced NOTHING reached the parent as an EMPTY tool result — a successful-looking call with no output (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1800** — the parent's tool result IS the child's final message, and `run_child` returned it verbatim. A child turn can end with no answer (the wall clock, the iteration budget or the grace gate can each stop it — the live incident behind iter-1783 ended a turn with `response_len=0`), and the delegation then reported SUCCESS with an empty string: the parent model could not act on it and could not tell it from a child that had nothing to say. **Fixed**: the finished turn is shaped in ONE place (`child_outcome`, shared by the sync, swarm-worker and background paths), and a child that produced no text is a NAMED failure ("The sub-agent finished its turn without producing any output"), not an empty result. Pinned by `tools::sub_agent_tool::tests::a_child_that_produced_no_output_is_a_failure_not_an_empty_result`, mutation-proved (dropping the check fails it by name) |
| RT-250 | An observer's post-execute envelope carried NULL arguments — the redaction seat it provides is a function of WHAT the tool was called with (found 2026-11-06) | **CLOSED iter-1803** — `ToolRegistry::execute` consulted the tool-seam interceptors' post-execute event with `args: Value::Null`. The documented envelope is (point, tool, args, result, config) and the docs promise args at every point, so the shipped behaviour contradicted the contract; and it crippled the named use case — the `replace` verdict an observer returns here is the redaction/enrichment seat (gap G2), and a redactor that can see the output but not the arguments cannot decide whether the output echoes what was passed in. **Fixed**: the call's args ride the post-execute envelope too (they already rode the pre-execute event, so no new surface is exposed to the same observer). Pinned by `tools::tests::post_execute_carries_the_args_the_tool_was_called_with` — a Replace verdict keyed on the args now lands in the result; mutation-proved (restoring `Value::Null` fails it with the unreplaced `{"result":"Processed: secret"}`) |
| D-5b | Live data loss on mainline | accepted limit — cron emits no memory session-boundary signal |
| D-6 | Live data loss on mainline | accepted limit — per-agent sub-agent budgets are process-global statics; cron runs jobs sequentially |

The last two are not checkboxes (their rows are `### D-5b` / `### D-6`
headings), so a reader who counts `- [ ]` sees the RT rows and misses two more.
S2 is likewise not a checkbox — it now has an index row above (added by the
2026-10-29 correction, when it was found missing). The count is measured by
`rg -c '^- \[ \]' docs/audit/2026-06-19-BUGS.md`; **at the 2026-10-29
correction that is 4** (RT-136, RT-190, RT-179, RT-197), against **285 closed**.
Every earlier number this paragraph carried — six, seven, nine — was a snapshot
that went stale, which is why the number now travels with the command.
