### Validation of the RT-205 withdrawal (iter-1567) — the withdrawal was PARTLY wrong, and the part that survives is a real defect I cannot yet localise

A validation pass over my own iter-1565 withdrawal. It was asked for and it
found that I withdrew too much. Recording all of it, including the part that
does not flatter me.

**The raw bytes refute my "stale viewport tail" explanation.** I claimed the
per-row stray characters in `/tmp/rt/c0.txt` were a `tmux capture-pane -p -e`
partial repaint. Decomposing the row into styled runs with the raw bytes:

```text
\x1b[2m\x1b[38;2;80;80;80m  CLEANPROBE: alpha acknowledged.
\x1b[0m\x1b[38;2;200;200;195m  .
\x1b[39m
```

The extra `.` carries a **different, deliberate style** (the answer-text colour)
from the run it follows. A stale repaint cannot invent a fresh, semantically
correct style pair. All six affected rows share one signature exactly:
`text \x1b[0m` + new style + **the last character of `text`**. That is a render
seam emitting a run's final cell twice — once in its own style, once in the next
run's.

**And I found a second, reproducible instance of the same bug class.** In a
fresh live session, the advisory block rendered with its bold span **displaced
from the text it belongs to**:

```text
dim  -> "T"                 BOLD -> "he foll"    dim -> "owing is an aggregated ..."
dim  -> "arrive outdated — is"  BOLD -> "sued at ear"    dim -> "lier turns ..."
```

The plain capture (same pane, `-p` without `-e`) reads correctly:
`The following is an aggregated review...` and `arrive outdated — issued at
earlier turns.` So the TEXT is right and the **style attribution is wrong** —
the displaced window is offset from its word. This is the same class of bug as
the duplicated final character: a span-boundary defect.

**But the markdown pipeline is clean, and I can prove it.** Four new tests,
each mutation-proven, cover the shapes I saw live:

- `a_bold_span_stays_on_its_own_characters_across_a_wrap`
- `a_mid_word_bold_run_starting_after_a_dim_prefix_stays_put` — the exact
  dim+BOLD mid-word structure from the live rows; RED (`left: "lowing"`,
  `right: "owing"`) when the window is displaced one character, restored
  byte-identical (md5 `44c59703df409c3e8047d6898715889c` both sides) and green
- `emphasis_offsets_survive_the_source_text_that_produced_the_live_rows` — goes
  through the real `render_markdown_with_width`
- `streaming_a_styled_paragraph_never_displaces_its_style_runs` — streams the
  same paragraph in 3-9 char fragments through `IncrementalMarkdownRenderer`
  and asserts every intermediate render is a prefix of the source

All 127 `operant_markdown::tests::cases` pass. So the wrap, the emphasis parser,
the full renderer AND the streaming renderer all keep style runs on the right
characters. The incremental renderer is the safest of these by design — its own
comment records that checkpoint-splicing was removed because it "caused
transient streaming artifacts like duplicated/misaligned content", so it does a
full re-render every update.

**Therefore the displacement is NOT in the markdown pipeline.** It is
downstream, in whichever layer converts already-styled `Line`s into cells for a
specific overlay — and the two places it shows up (the rewind selector body and
the reasoning-trace rows) both go through `prepare_body_for_overlay`. That is a
narrowing, not a fix: I have the defect class, a mutation-proven guard for the
markdown half of it, and an unexamined overlay layer.

**Honest ledger correction.** RT-205 should not have been closed. The correct
state is: the "duplicated character" observation was REAL in part — the
explanation I gave for it was wrong. Retracting the row means retracting my

### iter-1567 validation, second round — one guard rejected as a false positive, one kept

The validation pass found a defect in my own new test, which is the more useful
outcome. Recording both halves.

**A detection rule I invented was WRONG and I rejected it.** My first version of
the overlay guard asserted "no symbol may carry two different styles on one
row". Running it against the CLEAN, unmutated frame produced **10 conflicts** —
every shared letter between operant's gold banner text and the dim body text
(`n`, `t`, `e`, `r`, `o` in both). That rule fires on completely normal
rendering, so it is not a defect detector. Worse, it produced a convincing
"mutation proof": against the mutated frame it read `left: 11, right: 0`, which
looked like proof but was almost nothing, because the baseline was already 10.
A rule whose unmutated value is near its threshold cannot prove anything about
a change.

**The rule that survived is narrower and honest.** The kept assertion is the
one the live signature actually implies: a phrase must appear exactly ONCE in
the painted body. Mutation-proven by duplicating the phrase in the source, which
turns it RED with `left: 2, right: 1`; restored byte-identical
(md5 `81e1946881930b8cfbb3319a69015834` both sides) and GREEN.

**And the TestBackend cell grid cannot represent the live defect at all, which
is a real limitation and not a failure.** The live signature is
`text` + reset + new style + **the last character of `text`**, which is adjacent
in the ESCAPE STREAM. In the cell grid the prompt row's trailing padding cells
sit between the text's last cell and any appended cell, so an inserted duplicate
is never adjacency-adjacent to its original and the adjacency check cannot fire.
I verified this by instrumenting the mutation: `rows_touched=1` (the mutation
landed) with `adjacent_style_repeat=0`. So a cell-grid test can prove the body
does not duplicate TEXT, but it cannot prove the writer does not duplicate a
run's final CELL. That second claim needs the escape-stream level, which the
TestBackend does not expose.

Kept anyway, with its scope stated in the test's own doc comment, because it is
a real regression guard for the text-duplication half of the defect and it is
mutation-proven for that half. What it does NOT cover is recorded here rather
than overclaimed.

### iter-1575 validation — the "displaced bold" claim was an INFERENCE I could not substantiate, and a fifth false-positive rule rejected

I was asked to correct anything stale or overstated in my own work. The most
overstated item is one sentence in the RT-205 reopening: I called the advisory
block's bold span "displaced from the text it belongs to." I never saw the source
markdown for it. The advisory block comes from the runtime background-review path
and is NOT persisted — I verified this against the operator's real 107 MB
`~/.operant/database.db`:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE content LIKE '%aggregated review%';        -- 0
SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE content LIKE '%ADVISOR_CONTINUATION%';     -- 0
SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE content LIKE '%arrive outdated%';          -- 0
```

while my own probe prompts in the same session ARE persisted
(`OVERPROBE` 1, `RT205SECOND` 1, `RT205THIRD` 1, `PROBE alpha` 2). So the session
is reconstructable except for the one message the claim rests on. **Without that
source, "displaced" is a guess about which word the emphasis was on.** The claim
is withdrawn: the fact I actually observed is only that bold spans did not align
with the words I assumed they belonged to.

**A fifth false-positive rule, rejected for the third distinct reason.** I tried
to replace the inference with a measurement by rendering a REAL persisted message
(the 6.5 KB `**Timestamp:**` report) and asserting the bold text must be wrapped
in `**`. Rejected, because headings render bold without markers. Corrected to allow
headings — rejected, because the renderer legitimately splits spans around
punctuation so single characters arrive in bold runs. Corrected to a subsequence
invariant ("painted text must be a subsequence of markup-stripped source") —
rejected, because the real message contains `glob *.md` inside a table cell,
where `*` is a LITERAL GLOB CHARACTER and the renderer correctly keeps it. Any
filter that strips `*` from the source breaks; any filter that does not breaks on
genuine emphasis.

That is not a test I can keep patching: distinguishing a literal `*` from an
emphasis `*` is exactly the renderer's job, so a test asserting the painted text
matches a hand-stripped source must duplicate the renderer's parser to be right.
The rule was reverted (`git checkout`) and no claim is carried forward from it.

**What I should have done first and did not.** I asserted a rendering defect from
one capture without (a) retrieving the source that produced it, or (b) checking
the claim against a real message from the operator's own database. Both were
available in a minute each. The corrected ledger state for RT-205 is narrower and
less flattering than the reopening: **the only directly-evidenced symptom is the
raw-byte duplication of a run's final character under a new style**, and even that
is unexplained — four downstream homes (markdown parser, wrap, full renderer,
streaming renderer) are proven clean by 4 mutation-proven tests, and the cell-grid
harness cannot represent the escape-stream-level signature.

### RT-206 (NEW, found while closing "branching" in the exhaustive sweep) — Ctrl+B's `CurrentBranch` filter has no real anchor in production

The last unverified surface was `f` filter, compaction previews, the silent
`REHYDRATE_BYTES_BUDGET` truncation, and branching. The first three are now closed
(iter-1578, iter-1579 and the compaction notice, which is correct and correct
by test). The branching surface yielded a genuine defect.

`Ctrl+B` opens the session hub and sets `filter_mode = CurrentBranch` with
`branch_root = None`. The filter's job is "this branch's tree" — but the anchor
is resolved later, in `replace_rows`:

```rust
if self.branch_root.is_none() {
    self.branch_root = rows.iter()
        .find(|r| matches!(r.status, RowStatus::Live))
        .map(|r| r.id.clone());
}
```

**`RowStatus::Live` is assigned in exactly ONE production site:**
`operant-core/src/tools/async_delegation.rs`, for a row whose delegation is
`AsyncDelegationStatus::Pending`. The operator's own current session is built by
`Database::list_sessions_rich(500)`, which never marks anything Live — its rows
load as `RowStatus::Idle`. So there are two failure modes, both measured:

1. **No pending subagent** → `branch_root` stays `None` → the filter's match arm
   is `None => true` → **every session in the hub is shown**, under a header
   that says "this branch's tree". The operator pressed Ctrl+B and saw the
   whole hub instead of their branch.
2. **A pending subagent exists** → `branch_root` becomes the SUBAGENT's row →
   the filter narrows to that background delegation's branch, not the
   operator's conversation.

Both are pinned by `ctrl_b_with_no_live_row_lets_the_branch_filter_show_every_session`
and `a_pending_subagent_row_is_not_the_current_branch_anchor` in
`crates/operant-cli/src/tui/session_hub/tests.rs`. The second is mutation-proven:
deleting the auto-anchor block turns it red with `left: None, right:
Some("sub-1")` and the source was restored byte-identical (md5
`90a8705ba78449a0c3041288cc8fc7cd` both sides).

**The first test does NOT go red under that mutation, and that is deliberate and
recorded:** it asserts the unanchored defect itself (all three rows visible), so
removing the anchor cannot break it. It pins behaviour; the second test provides
the mutation sensitivity. Recording that here so a future agent does not mistake
a green mutation run for a passing guard.

NOT FIXED in this iteration: the fix needs an anchor source the App actually
has. `replace_rows` reads `self.rows` for the Live lookup but `self.rows` is
empty on the FIRST call (the rows are assigned after the anchor), so a
"first row" fallback is a no-op — I tried it as a mutation and it changed
nothing. The honest options are (a) have the loader mark the current session
Live (the App knows its own id), or (b) have Ctrl+B pass the live session id
into `branch_root` directly. Both touch the hub's load path, which the peer
agent is working in, so this is recorded rather than edited mid-flight.

### RT-207 (NEW) — two `tui::app::tests` fail on test ORDER, not on parallelism

Observed during the post-push full-workspace gate: 2 (occasionally 3) tests in
`crates/operant-cli/src/tui/app/tests.rs` fail on a full `cargo test`, but each
PASSES when run alone:

- `tui::app::tests::live_tails_render_once_while_a_tool_is_reserved`

- alone → both pass
- full binary suite in parallel → 2-3 failures, and the COUNT varies between
  runs (3, then 2)
- full binary suite with `--test-threads=1` → the same 2 fail, so this is
  test-ORDER dependence, NOT a parallel race

Not mine, and here is the proof rather than an assertion: `git diff 7ee1ccc0
HEAD -- crates/operant-cli/src/tui/app/tests.rs` is a SINGLE pure insertion of
84 lines (the `the_f_filter_is_reachable_...` test from iter-1578), zero
removals. The two failing tests' source is byte-identical to the peer's commit.
A pure insertion between existing tests cannot change their logic; it can only
run earlier or later in the order, which is exactly the symptom.

The AGENTS.md documents the mechanism: several tests share process-global cells
(the `config_shim::reasoning_override` cell is the documented example, and its
tests must hold `reasoning_override_test_guard()`). When an earlier test leaves
a global set, a later test that assumes the default fails.

**CLOSED (RT-207, this session, mutation-proven).** The bisect I deferred turned
out to take 12 minutes, not an iteration. Facts, each measured:

- `tui::app::tests` alone, serial: **273/273 pass**. The full binary, serial:
  2 fail. So the polluter is OUTSIDE that module.
- Bisecting the binary's modules found `gateway_commands` as the polluter, and
  bisecting inside it found TWO separate seeders, one per broken reader:
  * `a_completed_delegation_shows_its_result_and_a_failed_one_its_error`
    (seeds a completed + a failed record) breaks
    `highlight_covers_only_the_text_a_copy_carries`
  * `a_pending_delegation_is_named_running_and_shows_its_id_model_and_goal`
    (seeds a PENDING record) breaks
    `live_tails_render_once_while_a_tool_is_reserved`
- Both leak into the process-global delegation registry
  (`async_delegation.rs`, `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap>>`, **no clear path in
  production**). The leaked rows become `SessionEntryV2` subagent rows through
  `records_snapshot()` (`mod.rs:1451`), and render into later tests' frames.
- **Mechanism PROVEN, not inferred**: a temporary probe that cleared the
  registry immediately before the reader turned the failing pair GREEN
  (`2 passed, 0 failed`), where the identical pair is RED without it. Both
  probes were reverted byte-identical.

THE FIX: `RegistryDrain`, an RAII guard that empties the registry on drop
(`async_delegation.rs`), used by the two seeding tests. Clearing on DROP rather
than on construction matters — the seeding test must still see its own records
while it runs.

MUTATION-PROVEN BOTH WAYS: removing the pending-seeder's drain turns the reader
red again with exactly the recorded symptom (`left: 0, right: 1` — the reader's
own TEXTMARK text missing from the frame entirely, which is a WORSE symptom than
a duplicate). Source restored byte-identical (md5
`74d83f7278e8370f98101e2f501857ba`).

Full binary suite after the fix: **1952 passed, 0 failed** (two consecutive
green runs, then a single unrelated order-flake in
`model_pick_drain_switches_the_agent_and_persists` which passes alone and in its
module — pre-existing order-dependence, not this change, which is 65 insertions
and 0 deletions).

Ten `operant-core` failures on a full run are NETWORK tests binding localhost
ports (`gateway::slack::tests`, `gateway::webhook_subscriptions::tests`,
`error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:PORT)`); they do not reference
`async_delegation` and are unrelated. Recorded so a future reader does not
attribute them to this fix.

### RT-208 (NEW) — a test wrote `model = "new-model"` into the operator's live `~/.operant/operant.toml`

**The incident, observed live.** The flaky
`tui::app::commands::tests::model_pick_drain_switches_the_agent_and_persists`
writes a temp `operant.toml` with `model = "old-model"`, loads it, and drives
`persist_config_key("agent.model", "new-model")`. At 17:59 the operator's REAL
`~/.operant/operant.toml` came back with `model = "new-model"` — a test's
value — and every live turn failed with "no available keys" until the file was
restored from the backup at `/tmp/rt/operant.toml.damaged`. The repo's own
README claim that this is "only a test flake" is wrong: it is a test that
mutates the operator's live configuration.

**The mechanism — and why fixing HALF of it does nothing.**
`persist_config_key` writes into the process-global `LOADED_CONFIG_PATH`
(`config.rs`). TWO functions overwrite that global: `load_app_config` AND
`parse_config_str`, which `load_app_config` calls internally (config.rs:2482,
before the loader's own record). Two tests each loading a temp config race, and
the loser's surgical write lands in whichever path won.

My first fix guarded only the recorder inside `load_app_config`. The
regression test immediately proved it insufficient: `left:
Some(theirs.toml), right: Some(mine.toml)`. The concurrent load still won
because `parse_config_str` had already written the global before the loader's
guard ever ran. **Both writers now route through one helper**,
`record_loaded_config_path`, which defers to a peer's held guard.

**Two Rust traps that each silently defeated a correct-looking fix:**

1. **`let _g = f();` with an opaque return type is a temporary.** The guard
   factory returned `impl Deref + 'static`, so binding it with `let _g = ...`
   made Rust drop it at the end of the STATEMENT — the lock was released
   immediately and the guard granted nothing. It now returns the named
   `ConfigPathTestGuard` struct, which lives for the block.
2. **A Mutex is not reentrant.** A plain "skip while held" rule then stopped the
   HOLDER from recording its own load, so its guarded `persist_config_key`
   wrote into whatever a previous test left. A per-thread `CONFIG_PATH_HELD`
   cell now distinguishes "held by me" from "held by a peer": the holder
   records, peers defer. `Drop` clears it.

**MUTATION-PROVEN TWICE** (each revert -> red, source restored byte-identical,
md5-verified):

1. revert `parse_config_str`'s writer to ignore the guard ->
   `left: Some(theirs.toml), right: Some(mine.toml)`
2. drop the per-thread marker -> the 4 guarded persist tests all fail

**FIX iter-1588** (`0ee25f97`). Guarded callers: the 4 `config::tests` persist
tests plus `model_pick_drain_switches_the_agent_and_persists` (the flaky test
that caused the incident). operant-core config suite: **44/44 green**, scoped
clippy clean.

**THE `#[serial]` LESSON, recorded so the next guard is not built wrong.**
`#[serial]` serialises inside ONE test binary only. The damaging race was
between `operant-core`'s and `operant-cli`'s test modules in the same PROCESS,
which `#[serial]` cannot see. A test-global needs a real process-global lock,
not an attribute.

**TWO CLAIMS THIS ROW MAKES ABOUT ITS OWN VERIFICATION:**

1. The `operant-cli` half is NOT compile-verified. That binary does not compile
   in this tree, so the `commands.rs` guard could not be tested. Both errors
   belong to the peer's uncommitted WIP, not shipped code:
   `tui/app/mod.rs:1088` calls `operant_core::tools::todo_list_for_session`,
   which exists NOWHERE in the workspace, and `ui_messages.rs:990` matches
   `Self::Current { todos, plan, goals }` while the variant gained a 4th field.
   Recorded as feed F0246 to @agent-omarchy; not fixed here (fleet rule 7).
   The peer's WIP bytes are backed up byte-identical at
   `/tmp/rt/peer_mod_wip.rs` (md5 `86224bfdb2527b4c994894f3385fcecd`) — the
   temporary stub I used to compile past it was reverted that way.
2. **This fix landed under the wrong commit message.** The peer's
   `docs(iter-1588)` at `0ee25f97` swept both of my files into its commit while
   I was mid-commit, and that commit is ALREADY PUSHED to `origin/main`. The
   code is intact and correct on `origin/main` (verified:
   `record_loaded_config_path`, `ConfigPathTestGuard`, `CONFIG_PATH_HELD` all
   present at the pushed blob); only the message describes docs work. Per the
   append-only rule the published history is NOT rewritten — this row, plus the
   next `docs(iter-1589)` row, is the audit trail for it. This is the third
   time a peer's shared-index commit has carried my work; the fix is the same
   every time — verify what landed, then record it here.
- [x] **RT-208 (M, TEST MUTATED THE OPERATOR'S LIVE CONFIG).** Recorded as
  CLOSED above. The defect: `persist_config_key` writes into the process-global
  `LOADED_CONFIG_PATH`, and BOTH `load_app_config` AND `parse_config_str`
  (called inside it) overwrite that global, so parallel tests race and the
  loser's surgical write lands in the operator's real `~/.operant/operant.toml`.
  Observed live: the operator's config came back with `model = "new-model"` at

  both writers route through `record_loaded_config_path`, which defers to a
  peer's held `config_path_test_guard()`; a per-thread `CONFIG_PATH_HELD` cell

### RT-206 — CORRECTED: the iter-1587 fix was INCOMPLETE, and live testing is what found it

**The correction, and why it matters more than the original fix.** iter-1587
(`796c3ac1`) stored the App's own session id in `App::current_session` and
passed it to Ctrl+B's `CurrentBranch` filter. The pair of
mutation-proven tests passed, and the ledger recorded RT-206 CLOSED. **Live
verification against the freshly-built binary refuted that**: with one probe
instrumenting the keypress, `anchor=None` at Ctrl+B — the field was still
empty.

The mechanism, MEASURED not guessed: `agent.session_id()` returns **`None` at
adapter construction**. The agent's session id is minted by the FIRST TURN, and
a plain `operant chat` start has had none yet. So a field seeded at
construction is `None` exactly when the operator is most likely to press
Ctrl+B. I even tried seeding it at construction first and measured the probe
line `interactive seed agent.session_id()=None app.current_session=None` — the
fix was wrong on its own terms before I ever shipped it.

**Why a unit test could not catch it.** The existing test built its own state
(`app.current_session = Some("s-operator")`) and called the handler, so the
handler's read looked correct. The defect was never in the handler — it was in
the READER's timing, which no unit test exercises unless it explicitly
arranges for the reader to be non-None while the remembered field is None.

**THE FIX**: `SessionSwitchSource` gained a third closure — the agent's
`session_id()` reader — and Ctrl+B reads it live, falling back to the
remembered field. The agent is the only authority on the attached session.
Both construction sites (interactive and headless simulator) wire the same
closure.

LIVE-MEASURED before the fix, on `operant chat` with the real
`~/.operant/database.db` (the operator's 3214 sessions):

| filter | rows |
|---|---|
| `[this branch's tree]` | 19 |
| `[all]` | 19 (identical ids) |

LIVE-MEASURED after the fix, same database, after one real turn:

| filter | rows |
|---|---|
| `[this branch's tree]` | **1** (`#sess_d8ba7a6`) |
| `[all]` | **19** |

A probe note on measurement: my first post-fix probe reported 0 rows and I
nearly recorded the fix as over-narrowing. Two capture methods at the same
instant settled it — the row-count regex matched only lowercase-hex ids, and
this session's id (`#sess_d8ba7a6`) contains a `d` and a `6` in a shape the
pattern missed. **The observation was the defect, not the fix.**

**MUTATION-PROVEN**: reverting the one anchor line to
`branch_root = self.current_session.clone()` turns the new test red with
`left: None, right: Some("sess-live-from-agent")`. Source restored
byte-identical (md5 `6a447abf4ac590642694ba9a8977ea2e`).

CLOSED, RT-206. Fixed in this iteration. See the updated checkbox row above.

### Local provider gateway port drift: config and docs say 20129, the live server serves 20128 (2026-11-01)

**This is environment drift, NOT a code defect — no fix is owed to operant.**
Recorded because it silently blocked every live turn for a whole session.

The symptom looked exactly like "the gateway is down". `curl 000` on
`http://localhost:20129/v1/models`, `operant run` failing with "no available
keys", live TUI turns dying. Nothing on the port: `ss -tlnp` showed a listener on
`127.0.0.1:20128` and nothing on `20129`.

The diagnosis was one digit. An `aroute` process (`~/.local/bin/aroute --config
~/.config/ar/config.yaml serve`, up since 2026-10-30 09:01) was healthy and
serving on **:20128**, answering `/v1/models` with 200 and completing real
`small-stack` requests. Meanwhile `~/.operant/operant.toml` sets
`base_url = "http://localhost:20129/v1"` — matching `AGENTS.md:1090` and
`docs/RUNBOOK.md:36`, which both document 20129. So the config is behaving as
documented and the *server* is the half that moved, and no doc followed it.

Non-destructive workaround used throughout: `OPENAI_BASE_URL`
(`config.rs:3073` — one documented override that beats `operant.toml`) rather than
editing the operator's config. A live turn then succeeded in 3s against the real
`~/.operant/database.db`.

**For the next agent:** a `curl 000` on the documented port does NOT prove the
provider is down. Check `ss -tlnp` for the actual listener before reporting a
provider outage, and try both `OPENAI_BASE_URL` ports. Fixing the drift is an
owner call — either pin `aroute` back to 20129, or update `operant.example.toml`
/ `AGENTS.md` / `docs/RUNBOOK.md` together so they stop advertising a port that
nothing serves.

run boundary — and the frame holds 32 emphasis-carrying cells.

### RT-205 REPRODUCED, and iter-1606's verdict REFUTED (2026-11-01, this session)

**Iter-1606 recorded: "the signature does not reproduce on the deployed binary."
That record is WRONG and is refuted here. What follows supersedes it.**

The iter-1606 capture (`/tmp/rtstyle/dump60.txt`) never opened the rewind
overlay. Proof from its own bytes: it contains no `Rewind to a previous prompt`,
no `Rewind to here`, no `turns below dropped` — and it captured
`⠋ sending… 0s` + `A turn is running`, i.e. the first turn was still streaming
and never completed. A detector run against a frame with no overlay and no
assistant answer says nothing about the overlay. The "positive control" I claimed
in that entry (a run boundary where a doubled final character would land) was a
plain-transcript row, not a dimmed overlay row. Both the negative and its control
were hollow.

**Why the turns never completed:** the earlier simulator runs had no completed
turn, so `app.messages` had no turns to outline, so the overlay could not open at
all. The interactive TUI could not be used either: it rejects the local gateway
(`Authentication with the AI provider failed` for a dummy key), and `.env` holds
no `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

**The instrument that works: `operant tui debug simulate --agent-script <JSON>`.**
It injects mock agent events deterministically and offline
(`[{"type":"content","text":"..."},{"type":"done","text":"..."}]`), so turns
COMPLETE, `app.messages` fills, and `Esc Esc` opens the real overlay. This is the
missing capability that made every earlier live probe vacuous.

**THE DEFECT, reproduced with a control.** Over a 4-turn transcript with the
rewind overlay open, the LAST dimmed prompt row reads:

    4› delta four lazy sleeps nowck

`ck` is painted in `rgb:FF96C8/reset/b` — the pink-bold model-badge style —
while the row's own content is `rgb:505050/rgb:232832/b+d`. There is no `ck` in
the prompt. With 1-character prompts the same row reads:

    4› ddel to switch · Small Stack

— the prompt truncated to `delt` and the tail of the boot-banner line
`/model to switch · Small Stack` concatenated into the same row.

**Root cause, proven by comparing the two captures at the same row:**

| row | WITHOUT the overlay open | WITH the overlay open |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | ` operant` | ` operant` (identical) |
| 17 | ` /model to switch · Small Stack` | `4› delta four lazy sleeps now` + `ck` |
| 18 | ` v0.3.0` | ` v0.3.0` (identical) |

Row 17 held the boot banner. The overlay redraws that row with shorter content,
and the banner's surviving cells are never cleared: the new text overwrites
`Sta`, and `ck` (cols 29-30) is left behind in the banner's own style. The leak's
start column tracks the prompt length (col 20 for a 1-char prompt, col 29 for a
26-char one), which rules out a header-overflow cause and confirms stale cells at
a fixed offset past the new content's end.

**Control:** with the overlay closed, no prompt row carries a foreign-styled cell
(0 hits). With it open, 1 hit on the last body row. Stable across all 194 overlay
frames, so it is not a transient repaint artifact. No shipped
`tui_scenarios/baselines/*.style.txt` golden shows it, so it is not an accepted
appearance.

**CORRECTIONS to two claims I made on the way, both recorded because each read
as authoritative before it was measured:**

1. My first root-cause reading — "`ui_header.rs:727` pushes the model-name span
   unconditionally while the hint and prefix are width-guarded" — was WRONG. That
   site formats a display NAME and is not in the overlay's render path at all.
2. My second reading — "`ui_header.rs` is a 1704-line name formatter, so the real
   cause is the *stale cell buffer*" — was closer but still imprecise, and the fix
   I wrote from it did not work. See below.

**This is the RT-205 shape exactly**: a row's content surviving into a new frame
under a DIFFERENT style, emitted past the end of the new run — which is the
original live signature (`1› CLEANPROBE one alpha` + `a`, `▸ thought` + `t`) and
the mechanism the repo's own instrument
(`the_overlay_body_does_not_emit_a_spans_final_character_twice`) was built to
catch. FIXED in the iteration that follows.

The TestBackend hazard is IDENTICAL to the live one and a unit test CAN catch
this — the succeeding section proves it. `TestBackend::draw` writes only the cells
it is given (`backend/test.rs:252-260`) and `Terminal::try_draw` diffs against the
previous buffer; ratatui's own contract: "each frame is compared to the previous
frame... If the render function does not fully render the frame, the terminal will
not be in a consistent state." Two conditions were needed and neither held in the
repo's instruments: (a) the overlay must open over a frame that already has content
in those rows, and (b) the second frame must go through `render_app` — driving
`draw_rewind_selector` directly does NOT reproduce it, MEASURED, because
`Paragraph`'s `buf.set_style(text_area, self.style)` resets the style across the
whole text area and the isolated call happens to be clean.

### RT-205 FIXED, with a mutation-proven test and a second fix that did not work (iter-1607)

**The fix.** `crates/operant-cli/src/tui/rewind_selector.rs`, in
`draw_rewind_selector`: the body `Paragraph` now writes **every cell of its
area** — each `mid` line is padded to the area's full width, and the line count is
padded to the body height with rows of real spaces. Rationale: the selector is a
FULLSCREEN surface (its paint site passes `ctx.size`), so it owns the whole area,
and ratatui's `render_line` writes only a line's own graphemes.

**The fix that did NOT work, recorded because the reason is generalizable.** My
first attempt padded only each line's width. The leak was unchanged. The
second attempt padded the line *count* with `Line::from("")` — still unchanged.
An empty line has no graphemes, so `render_line` writes no cells for it at all and
the row keeps whatever the previous frame left there. MEASURED both times: rows
16-26 still held frame one's banner, model line and status bar. The pad rows must
contain actual spaces. This is the same trap as the vacuous test: an action that
looks like it fills an area but writes nothing.

**The test.** `crates/operant-cli/src/tui/app/tests.rs`,
`opening_the_rewind_selector_erases_the_previous_frames_cells`. It paints frame
one through `render_app` (the app's real chrome), then opens the selector and
paints frame two the same way, then asserts that **no row in the overlay's body
region carries a colour the overlay's dim ramp never uses**. The scope is derived
from the overlay's own markers (header row, caption row, footer row), not guessed.

Two earlier drafts of that assertion were wrong and are recorded: counting
"distinct styles > 2" flagged the app's legitimately multi-styled status row and
would have failed even with the fix in place; and an earlier scope
(`r < first -- INSERT row`) computed the whole area, so it flagged that same status
row. The detector is now the precise one: a non-padding cell whose fg is not the
overlay's `rgb:505050` dim ramp.

**MUTATION PROOF (both directions, md5-verified):**

| `rewind_selector.rs` | result |
|---|---|
| fixed `8637c622` | PASS (2 tests) |
| padding removed | FAIL, naming 9 leaked rows: 16 ` operant · replay · perf:reduced`, 17 ` operant`, 18 ` /model to switch · api-key:openai · GPT-4`, 19 ` v0.3.0`, 20 ` /login to add provider`, 21 ` ● openai(key)`, 22 the cwd line, 25 `5>`, 26 the status bar |
| restored `8637c622` | PASS (2 tests) |

**Live A/B, same build pipeline, on the deployed binary's code path:**

| build | result |
|---|---|
| no padding | row 15 `3› gamma three fox jumps highced`, row 17 `4› delta four lazy sleeps nowck` |
| with padding | NO LEAK |

**The gate is not free of pre-existing red:** one
`tui::operant_ui::pinned_ui::tests::render_side_panel_markdown_without_native_protocol_shows_mermaid_source`
failure exists WITH and WITHOUT this change (verified by stashing it), in the
peer's mermaid subsystem. Recorded, not fixed (fleet rule 7).

**RT-205's row is amended to CLOSED by this fix** — see the surviving row above,
whose signature this mechanism reproduces exactly. The row stays listed so the
full chain of false starts and the corrections to them remain readable.

## OPEN — the rewind selector's caption carries a stale cell after a filter close (found 2026-11-02, iter-1665)

- [x] **RT-211 (M, RENDER) — the selector's `⏪ Rewind to here …` caption left a
  stale character in the wide glyph's continuation cell. CLOSED iter-1685.**
  **iter-1685 correction of the root cause below (measured, supersedes it): the
  `buffer_rows` / style-dump reading was a red herring, and the earlier column
  arithmetic was right for the wrong reason.** The defect is in the RENDER, not
  the probe: closing the filter shrinks the header from two rows to one, so the
  caption's row slides UP onto the row that previously held `  filter: `.
  Ratatui's `Paragraph` diff writes a wide grapheme at its column and treats the
  NEXT cell as its continuation WITHOUT rewriting it, so the caption's second
  space is served from that stale continuation cell — the filter field's `i` is
  then visible, and the whole caption sits one column right of where it belongs.
  Proven with two frames on ONE `TestBackend`, both through
  `draw_rewind_selector` (the production path), then narrowed by a control that
  swaps ONLY the marker width and renders correctly. Fix: a NARROW marker
  (`>>`), one cell wide, so the diff rewrites every column the line covers.
  Regression `the_rewind_caption_survives_a_filter_close` is mutation-proven
  (restoring the wide glyph fails it with `"  ⏪i Rewind to here …"` in the
  message). The two goldens that carried the wide glyph were refreshed, as this
  row required. **Original finding (2026-11-02):** Open the selector,
  type a filter, press Enter to close it: the caption renders
  `"  ⏪i Rewind to here …"` where it should read `"  ⏪  Rewind …"`. Reproduced
  deterministically on the deployed binary with
  `<esc><esc>fsecond<enter><up>`; the unfiltered `<esc><esc><up>` path is
  correct. Root cause is isolated to the cell level: `⏪` (U+23EA) is a WIDE
  glyph occupying two cells, and `buffer_rows()` (`tui/debug/debug_hub.rs:474`)
  reads `c.symbol()` per cell — the style dump at that position is the correct
  empty continuation cell (`rgb:BA8BFF/reset/-@`), so the TestBackend's *cell*
  still holds the `i` from the previously drawn `filter: …` line. Writing the
  caption does not clear the cell the wide glyph's left half now covers.
  Pre-existing and not caused by this iteration's work: the caption string was
  introduced by the peer's iter-1589 (`8263e8e8`). Note the golden I added in
  iter-1661 (`rewind-selector-populated-filter`) faithfully RECORDS the bad
  cell, which is why fixing this bug will require a golden refresh — and the
  refresh is the proof it was fixed. Not fixed here: it is a real defect in the
  peer-owned caption, and the fix must land with a golden update in one
  iteration so the corpus does not pin the bug as correct.

## CLOSED — the TUI's own test gate depended on the developer's shell (found 2026-11-05, iter-1746)

- [x] **RT-212 (M, GATE + DEAD GUARD) — four defects in the `operant-cli` test
  gate itself, found during the tui-bugfix campaign's phase-2 sweep. The suite
  was RED at tip for reasons unrelated to the code under test.**
  **(1) The palette assertions were environment-dependent.** Measured

  `cargo test -p operant-cli --bin operant` suite reported **9 failures** — four
  in `tui::theme_colors::tests` (`error`/`success`/`warning` accessors and
  `theme_palette_should_change_shared_render_colors`), three in
  `tui::operant_ui::composer::tests` (the band-fill trio) and
  `tui::overlays::layout::tests::modal_frame_leaves_the_surface_under_it_untouched`.
  Every one of them failed at the same seam: `color_depth::detect()` reads the
  AMBIENT environment, `NO_COLOR` has top priority in its decision table, and
  `quantize` maps every colour to `Color::Reset` at `ColorDepth::None`. So the
  developer's shell decided what the suite asserted. **Closed by iter-1746**:
  `detect()` now runs `detect_process()`, which in a test build takes its
  answer from the EXPLICIT override (`OPERANT_COLOR_DEPTH`) alone and otherwise
  defaults to `Truecolor` — which is the corpus's own pin
  (`_run.py`'s `PINNED_ENV`), so the unit suite and the visual corpus now agree
  on the palette they assert against. The ambient probe is untouched in a real
  build, so the operator's `NO_COLOR` still yields no colour in the TUI.
  Pinned by two tests: the pure `detect_for_tests` table (default / override /
  explicit `none` / typo) and the process-level answer.
  **(2) The composer's palette tests read a global without its lock.**
  With the depth fixed, the band-fill suite failed differently in the FULL run
  while passing in isolation: the buffer was painted with NORD's surface
  (`Rgb(71,76,87)`) while the expectation read the default theme's
  (`Rgb(53,53,71)`) — the process-global palette changed between the two reads
  because the theme tests write it under the shared `ACTIVE_LOCK` and the
  composer tests did not take it. The render module and `app/tests.rs` already
  took that lock (RT-149's iter-1136 fix); the composer tests were the
  unlocked reader. **Fixed**: a `palette_guard()` helper in the same shape as
  `overlays/layout.rs`'s, taken by the four palette-reading tests.
  **(3) A test-only override was a stub, so its test asserted a state it never
  created.** `crate::tui::operant_app::mermaid::with_image_protocol_override`
  was the W9-cut stub `fn with_image_protocol_override<T>(_enabled: Option<bool>,
  f) -> T { f() }` — it ignored its argument. The side-panel mermaid test
  (`tui::operant_ui::pinned_ui::tests::render_side_panel_markdown_without_native_protocol_shows_mermaid_source`)
  has called it with `Some(false)` since iter-1608 to pin the source-fallback
  render, but the door it believed it closed stayed OPEN, so the native ASCII
  diagram rendered and the test failed — it was the known-red-at-tip failure
  `agent-omarchy` recorded for `jcode` in `F0269`. The real door is
  `operant_markdown::context`'s thread-local override, which the fallback's
  own re-export already reaches. **Fixed**: the stub forwards to it, so every
  caller of either spelling now pins the same door.
  **(4) A source guard carried no `#[test]` for 52 iterations.**
  `the_extraction_is_really_in_the_render_path_not_only_in_the_tests`

## CLOSED — the TUI's command sweep called a simulator that could not start 98 broken commands (found 2026-11-05, iter-1748)

- [x] **RT-214 (M, GATE) — `command_sweep.py` conflated "the command fell
  through to the model" with "the simulator did not run", and reported the
  second as the first.**
  **The measurement.** The sweep drives every registered command through
  `tui debug simulate --keys '/<cmd><enter>' --assert 'messages == 0'` and
  read ANY non-zero exit as a fall-through. In a sandbox whose HOME is
  read-only, the simulator cannot write its own state, exits non-zero for
  every command, and the sweep printed **`consumed: 0/98`** with all 98
  commands listed under "BROKEN (fall through to the model as prompt text)".
  Every one of those 98 commands dispatches correctly — with a writable HOME
  the same sweep prints `98/98` — so the report was 98 false defects, and a
  reader would have gone looking for them. This is the RT-162 shape: a gate
  whose failures are all one cause reports that cause once per case.
  **The fix, in three parts.**
  (1) **Three outcomes, not two.** The simulator's own failure text
  (`Assertion failed: messages == 0 (actual: N)`) separates a real
  fall-through from a run that died earlier; anything else is a SIMULATOR
  ERROR, reported under its own heading as "the command's behaviour is
  UNKNOWN, not broken". Both classes still exit non-zero: a gate that cannot
  verify must not pass.
  (2) **A hermetic run.** The sweep used the operator's real HOME, so their
  sessions, skills and slash-usage store were in scope and a read-only HOME
  made every command look broken. It now builds a fresh HOME + HERMES_HOME per
  sweep, pins `OPERANT_COLOR_DEPTH`/`TERM`/`PATH` the way the corpus does, and
  runs from the fixture directory rather than the operator's cwd.
  (3) **Its own regression test.** `scripts/tests/command_sweep_test.sh` drives
  two FAKE simulators — one that exits 1 without running, one that prints the
  assertion failure — and asserts each lands in its own class, that neither
  class is confused for the other, and that both exit non-zero. The test is
  wired into `scripts/self-test.sh`, because a check that runs only when a human
  remembers to run it is not a gate (the RT-162 lesson).
  **Verification:** the real binary now reports `consumed: 98/98`, exit 0, in
  the same sandbox where the old sweep reported 98 broken.

- [x] **RT-215 (M, VERIFICATION) — two defects in the TUI's own verification

  the last key (the base scenario's notes measured it: "the plain path
  coalesces and the final state never lands"). The scenario's own notes named

  and it is now `<wait:N>`: N frames with NO key applied, so queued content
  lands and the final frame settles. **N FRAMES, not milliseconds, on
  purpose:** a frame count is deterministic by construction, while a duration
  would put the corpus's verdict back on the machine's load — the exact defect
  the scenario was excluded for. The token is parsed in `parse_key_sequence`
  (a `<wait:N>` expands to N Null key events), the simulator skips a Null key
  without applying it (`apply_terminal_event`, gated on `is_simulating`, so the
  interactive path is untouched), and `_validate.py` learned the new grammar so
  the validator stops rejecting the scenario that uses it.

  gone, the landing assert is back (`contains:L001`, `not-contains:L199`), and
  its two goldens are committed. The ladder it now pins, measured through the
  corpus's own harness: **0 presses → L145, 1 → L085, 2 → L026, 3 → L001 (the
  ceiling), 4-6 → L001 (clamped)** — a monotonic climb that stops at the real
  ceiling, which is the third-press rung the variant was created to pin in
  iter-1200 and never could. **Mutation-proven:** reverting the scroll
  direction in `scroll_up_rows` (`saturating_sub` → `saturating_add`, the
  defect class that parks the reader at the tail) fails the scenario with
  "expected to contain 'L001'", and the base scenario fails with its own
  "expected to contain 'L020'"; the mutation was reverted and both are green.

## CLOSED — the scroll-back counter overwrote the transcript it was counting (found 2026-11-05, iter-1754)

- [x] **RT-218 (M, RENDER) — the ↓/↑ scroll counters were painted OVER the
  transcript's own text, so a reader scrolled back in history saw corrupted
  words instead of a counter.**
  **Measured, not inferred.** The corpus renders showed the counter's arrow
  with a LETTER on both sides of it — the shape that means "chrome ate a
  word": `scroll-pageup-moves-viewport` row 24 rendered
  `L039 scroll test↓40ne` (the " li" of "scroll test line" replaced by
  `↓40`) and `scroll-pageup-third-press` row 18 rendered `L032 s↓51ll`. A
  corpus-wide sweep for a symbol embedded between two alphanumerics found
  exactly these two hits (the third, `help-overlay`'s `none|minimal|…`, is a
  legitimate list separator).
  **Why.** The counters were painted at fixed ABSOLUTE rows — the ↓ counter at
  `render_area`'s last row, the ↑ counter at its first — while the transcript
  paints into `content_area`, which spans those rows whenever no top band is
  reserved (no pinned todos, no prompt preview). The counter therefore landed
  ON the last (or first) visible line and, because it is painted AFTER the
  transcript Paragraph, replaced that line's tail. `chat_native_scrollbar()`
  returns `false` unconditionally, so the counters are always the live path;
  nothing else covered them. The upstream jcode source carries the same
  geometry (a byte-identical port), so this is an inherited upstream defect
  rather than an operant regression — and it is still a defect here, because
  the operator reads the transcript.
  **Fixed.** The counters now paint only into a row's TRAILING WHITESPACE, and
  only where the counter fits: the ↓ counter searches from the last row UP
  (the rows the reader is looking at), the ↑ counter from the first row DOWN.
  A row with no room is skipped rather than truncated — the counter is a hint,
  the text is the content. The counter KEEPS its designed home (the area's
  right edge) whenever the row leaves that edge clear, and moves in behind the
  text only when the text reaches the edge — so a frame whose counter had
  room on the right keeps the exact position it had, and only the corrupting
  frames change. The layout is untouched: no row was reserved, so
  `max_scroll`, `visible_height`, the resize anchor and the copy viewport are
  all unchanged.
  **The rule is now a pure function** (`scroll_counter_placement`), which is
  what made the fix provable: a row hosts the counter only if the row's text
  leaves room for it at the counter's own column; the counter keeps its
  designed home (the render area's right edge, at the exact column the old
  formula computed, so an UNaffected frame keeps its pixels and its golden)
  and moves in behind the text only when the text reaches that edge. The ↓
  counter searches upward from the last row, the ↑ counter downward from the
  first.
  **Mutation-proven, in BOTH directions, by two tests.** The rule test
  (`the_scroll_counter_is_placed_where_it_cannot_cover_text`) fails when the
  room check is removed from the rule ("a row whose text leaves no room for
  the counter must be refused, not painted over"); the rendered-frame test
  (`the_scroll_counter_never_overwrites_transcript_text`) fails when the
  counter is suppressed entirely — the "fix by silence" shape — because its
  second arm asserts the counter is STILL drawn when a row has trailing room.
  Without that second arm a fix that merely stopped drawing the counter would
  pass.
  **Two earlier drafts of the frame test passed under the mutation**, and a
  probe found why each time: the first fixture used one message per line, and
  the renderer puts a BLANK row between messages, so the viewport's last row
  was blank and had room for anything; the second fixture's text was long
  enough to wrap but still left four free columns, and the counter fitted
  there. The defect needs the text to REACH the counter's column, so the
  frame test now sweeps three widths and asserts the words survive, and the
  rule test carries the exact geometry.
  **Verified in the real process:** after the fix the same two scenarios render
  `L031  ↓40` — the text intact, the counter beside it.

## CLOSED — the TUI's live-verification tool could not run its own documented recipe (found 2026-11-05, iter-1753)

- [x] **RT-217 (M, TOOL) — `scripts/tui-capture.sh` could not run the recipe
  `docs/library/tui-debugging.md` documents, and one of its failure modes
  silently produced a capture with its determinism controls stripped away.**
  **All three defects were found by RUNNING the tool, not by reading it.**
  **(1) A FAILED `mktemp` BECAME THE FILESYSTEM ROOT.** The script runs
  `set -uo pipefail` WITHOUT `-e`, so `PIN_HOME="$(mktemp -d ...)"` failing left
  the variable EMPTY, and every path below it became `/operant.toml` and
  `/.operant`. Measured 2026-11-05 with a `TMPDIR` that is not writable: the
  config write reports "Read-only file system", the child TUI starts with NO
  pinned config and a broken HOME — and the tool still prints
  "wrote ... capture (ANSI preserved)" and exits 0. **A capture that lost its
  determinism controls while reporting success is worse than no capture**,
  because the whole point of the file is that a developer's local theme,
  config and keybindings cannot leak in. It now fails loud (exit 2, the usage
  code) naming the TMPDIR that failed.
  **(2) THE WAIT WAS CHECKED WHERE IT COULD NEVER SUCCEED.** `--wait-text`
  polled the pane BEFORE the keys were typed, so the file's own example —
  `--keys '/help' --enter --wait-text 'Commands'` — timed out on every run:
  the overlay's text can only be on screen AFTER the command that opens it has
  been typed. The pre-key wait is now the quiescence strategy (the TUI must be
  up and quiet before it is driven) and the text wait runs after the submit,
  with its own timeout report. The recipe now completes in ~13 s instead of
  burning the full timeout and lying about it.
  **(3) THE DOC'S NEEDLES NAMED A SECTION THAT DOES NOT EXIST.**
  `docs/library/tui-debugging.md` used `Shortcuts` in three examples — the
  `--assert-screen` syntax example, the dialog-opening example and the live
  recipe. The help overlay's sections are `Commands`, `Session` and
  `Memory & Swarm`, and `baselines/help-overlay.txt` agrees with the live
  capture, so the overlay is the authority and the prose was stale. The live
  recipe waited for text that never arrives; its headless twin carried a
  SECOND trap the needle hid: with no credential pin the first-run "Connect a
  provider" dialog opens, it is MODAL, and it swallows the typed `/help` — the
  keys land in its search field, `overlays.help_overlay == false`, and the
  documented gate is red for a perfectly good overlay (measured live AND
  headlessly). All three needles are `Commands` now, the headless example
  pins the placeholder key the corpus and the live tool already pin, and both
  commands pass verbatim as written.

## CLOSED — the keybindings catalogue advertised a quit chord that nothing dispatched (found 2026-11-05, iter-1758)

- [x] **RT-218 (M, FALSE PROMISE) — `/keys` and `/hotkeys` have advertised
  `Ctrl+Q → Quit application` for the whole life of the Global table, and the
  chord did nothing.**
  **Measured, not inferred.** The catalogue entry is
  `key: KeyCode::Char('q'), modifiers: CONTROL, action: KeyAction::Cancel,
  description: "Quit application"`; a grep for a Ctrl+Q dispatch in
  `app/key_handling.rs` finds nothing — the only `Char('q')` arms are the
  overlay close handlers (bare `q` inside the plugins, journey and stats
  panes). The operator pressed the chord the help screen promised and the TUI
  ignored it. **Why no gate caught it:** the keybindings guard
  (`global_bindings_should_be_dispatched_in_key_handling`) asks whether the
  key TOKEN appears somewhere in the dispatch file, and `KeyCode::Char('c')`
  does — so a `Ctrl+X` entry is satisfied by an unrelated bare `x` press. The
  guard's own comment names this limit; it is the limit that hid the lie.
  **THE MECHANISM HAD A SECOND HALF, and that is the part worth keeping.**
  The exit confirmation is a two-press state machine split across two places:
  the arms call `handle_exit_key_confirmation` (start and complete the
  sequence), and a reset at the END of `handle_key_event` wipes the sequence
  for every key outside `{Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D}`. A chord the arms accept but that
  list does not name therefore has its own state cleared between the two
  presses — the sequence can never complete and the chord looks like it does
  nothing at all. Adding an arm alone would NOT have fixed this.
  **Fixed in three places that must agree:** the dispatch arm (Ctrl+Q arms the
  same confirmation, and unlike Ctrl+C it does NOT clear the composer — a
  chord pressed by accident must not destroy a typed prompt before the exit
  is confirmed); the reset list (now names every chord the confirmation
  accepts); and the confirmation message (it names the chord it is asking
  about, so the second press is unambiguous).
  **Two tests, one behavioural and one about the INVARIANT.**
  `ctrl_q_asks_for_confirmation_and_then_exits` drives the real key handler:
  the first press asks, the second exits. It was proved RED before the fix
  (it failed on the second press). `every_exit_chord_survives_the_key_handlers_reset`
  pins the invariant that every chord a confirmation arm accepts is named in
  the reset list, so the NEXT chord cannot repeat this by omission. Dropping
  `'q'` from the reset list fails BOTH tests (the invariant one names the
  chord, the behavioural one loses the exit).
  **Live evidence, and its limit.** In a real pty the first Ctrl+Q shows
  "Press Ctrl+Q again to exit", so the chord reaches the handler in a
  terminal. The second press does not terminate the app in this sandbox's
  tmux — and the SHIPPED Ctrl+C does not terminate there either (it shows no
  notice at all, so it never reaches the confirmation), which makes the
  two-press TERMINATION a unit-level fact and the live non-termination a
  pre-existing behaviour of the shipped chord in this environment rather than
  a regression from this change. The live difference between the two chords
  (Ctrl+Q reaches the handler, Ctrl+C does not) is measured and unexplained;
  it is the next thing to chase.
  **RESOLVED THE SAME ROUND (measured, and NOT a product defect):** the
  asymmetry is an instance of a class `keybindings/report.rs` ALREADY documents
  — `OS_CONFLICTS` names `Ctrl+c` ("SIGINT — the tty line discipline usually
  acts before the app sees it"), `Ctrl+q` ("XON — terminal software flow
  control resumes output") and `Ctrl+d` ("tty EOF (VEOF) — closes the input
  stream instead of paging"). `/keys` already warns the operator that these
  chords are commonly intercepted by the terminal, the window manager or the
  VM layer before the TUI sees them, so the catalogue was honest about the
  risk and the help screen already carries the warning. The live probe's
  asymmetry (Ctrl+Q reached the handler, Ctrl+C did not) is that documented
  interception class showing up in a tmux pane, not a defect in the dispatch.
  **So no further chase is owed on the asymmetry**: the real defects this row
  found were the missing dispatch arm and the reset list that could have
  completed it, and both are fixed and tested.

## CLOSED — the settings screen dropped an edited value, and its own guard never saw the row (found 2026-11-05, iter-1760)

- [x] **RT-219 (M, FALSE SAVE) — the `/settings` screen offered "File
  injection max size", the operator edited it, and the save DISCARDED it.**
  **The defect.** `all_entries` offers 19 editable settings;
  `apply_and_save` had **no case** for `fileInjectionMaxSize`, so the value
  rendered in the row, landed in `pending_changes`, and was dropped by the
  match — while the whole settings.json was rewritten from the snapshot, which
  carries the OLD `file_injection_max_size` forward. RT-171's defect class
  (the screen rewriting values it does not apply), one row over.
  **Why no gate caught it — the interesting half.** The file-injection rows are
  only OFFERED when file injection is enabled: `all_entries` pushes
  `fileAutocompleteLimit`, `fileAutocompleteShowHiddenFiles` and
  `fileInjectionMaxSize` under `if screen.file_injection_enabled`. The guard
  written for exactly this class,
  `every_settings_entry_has_an_applier`, derives its key list from
  `all_entries(&screen)` with the DEFAULT screen — where those three rows are
  not offered at all. So it checked SIXTEEN keys and the defect sat in the
  three it never saw. A guard that derives its list from the UI is only as
  complete as the UI STATE it derives it from.
  **Fixed in two places.** (1) `apply_and_save` applies the value
  (`settings.config.file_injection_max_size` — a `usize`, the same shape as its
  `fileAutocompleteLimit` sibling) and refreshes the row's own field so the
  screen and the file agree. (2) The guard checks BOTH screens — the default
  one AND one with file injection enabled — and ASSERTS that the second offers
  MORE rows, so the conditional coverage cannot quietly shrink again if the
  condition changes shape.
  **Tests.** A behavioural one walks the operator's real path: turn file
  injection on (the row appears), then edit the max size, then save. It was
  proved RED before the fix — "left: 0, right: 2048", the edited value
  dropped and the old one kept. Removing the new applier arm fails BOTH that
  test and the guard, which names the row.
  **Also in this iteration: two verification gaps closed.** (a) The
  keybindings guard's own "WHAT THIS DOES NOT CATCH" note said it could not see
  a MODIFIER — "a binding of `Ctrl+X` is satisfied by an unrelated bare `x`
  press" — which is exactly the hole iter-1758's Ctrl+Q defect fell through.
  `global_bindings_should_be_dispatched_with_their_modifier` now checks both
  dispatch shapes (an exact keycode with the modifier in its guard, and the
  generic `KeyCode::Char(c)` arm whose guard names the character AND the
  modifier), skipping only the one keycode crossterm folds the modifier into
  (`BackTab` = Shift+Tab). Deleting the Ctrl+Q arm fails it by name.
  (b) The TUI suite was FLAKY: `tui::render::tests::accent_role_reaches_the_frame`
  failed in 1 of 2 full-suite runs (green in isolation). The cause is
  measured: the scroll-counter test added at iter-1754 builds an `App`
  WITHOUT the shared palette lock, and `App::new` resets the PROCESS-GLOBAL
  palette — so it could reset it between the accent test's `set_active_theme`
  and its paint (the RT-149 class). That test now holds the lock for its whole
  body. **Measured after the fix: 5 of 6 full-suite runs green, and the accent
  test did not recur.** The sixth run failed a DIFFERENT test —
  `tui::app::tests::highlight_covers_only_the_text_a_copy_carries` — which is
  green 12/12 in isolation and 4/4 when its whole module runs alone, so it is
  a second, separate cross-test race (it diffs the STYLES of two consecutive
  renders, so anything that changes the frame between them reads as a
  selection highlight).
  **That second race is the SAME palette resetter, reached through a different
  path, and it is now fixed too (iter-1761).** `highlight_covers_only_the_text_a_copy_carries`
  reads the DIFFERENCE between two consecutive frames' styles, so a palette
  reset between the two renders changes the row's style and the difference
  reads as a selection highlight — the gutter assertion then fails on a
  perfectly good selection. The test now holds the shared palette lock across
  both renders. It takes the lock AFTER `make_app()` (which takes and releases
  the same mutex itself — holding it across `make_app` would deadlock).
  **Measured after both fixes: 5 of 5 full-suite runs green**, the accent test
  and the highlight test both absent from the failures, and the only failure
  seen is this sandbox's read-only HOME in
  `gateway_runner::tests::the_daemon_lock_survives_the_start_functions_return`
  (it passes with a writable HOME).

## CLOSED — the tips strip advertised three chords that no longer did what it said (found 2026-11-05, iter-1762)

- [x] **RT-220 (M, FALSE ADVICE) — the tips widget advertised three chords
  that no longer do what the tips say.** The tips strip is the one surface the
  operator reads ON A LOOP (it rotates every 15 seconds), so a stale chord
  there does not sit unread in a help screen: it sends the operator to the
  wrong feature while they are working.
  **Measured against the keybinding catalogue** (`/keys` is the same table):
  1. "Ctrl+G or Alt+G toggles a scroll bookmark" — **Ctrl+G is the EXTERNAL
     EDITOR** (the bookmark moved to Alt+G at iter-1267). Pressing the chord the
     tip named opened the operator's editor instead of the bookmark.
  2. "Ctrl+T enters drag-select copy mode" — **Ctrl+T toggles the THINKING
     DISPLAY** (copy mode moved from Ctrl+T to Alt+Y at plan 08).
  3. "PageUp / PageDown scroll 10 lines" — the live step is one PAGE (the
     transcript viewport's height minus two rows of overlap); 10 is only the
     fallback for a headless app that has published no frame.
  The module's own comment claimed every tip had been "verified against the
  keybinding registry / dispatch arms" — that sentence was false for three of
  the ten tips, which is why nothing caught them.
  **Fixed, and the class is closed.** The three tips now name the true chords
  (Alt+G, Alt+Y, "one page"), and
  `every_chord_a_tip_names_agrees_with_the_catalogue` pins each tip's prose
  to a row of a table whose third column is the CATALOGUE's own description for
  the chord — so the tip and the catalogue cannot drift apart unnoticed. The
  test also refuses any chord a tip names that the table does not pin, so a
  chord ADDED to a tip without a claim fails too. **Both old tips are caught:
  restoring the Ctrl+G tip fails with "the tip names Ctrl+G, which this test
  does not pin", and restoring the Ctrl+T tip fails with "no tip contains ...
  — the claim this test pins is gone".** The one tip that names a chord to say
  the operator does NOT need it (the copy-on-select advice mentions Ctrl+C) is
  exempt, with the reason in the code.

## CLOSED — two vendored messages pointed at commands operant does not have (found 2026-11-05, iter-1767)

- [x] **RT-223 (M, DEAD POINTER) — the strings were rebranded, the commands
  they name were not.** Two user-facing messages point at commands operant has
  never had:
  1. The CORE handler registry's `/tools` reply: "Available tools: memory,
     web_search, web_fetch, bash, and more. **Use /toolsets for the full
     list**." There is no `/toolsets` — it is in neither the TUI's command
     table nor the handler registry. The model that reads this reply tries a
     command that does not exist and asks again; the operator who reads it
     (same message, same transcript) has the same experience. Pointing at the
     MCP panel would not fix it: its tool pane holds the MCP SERVERS' tools,
     not the agent's own.
  2. The OpenAI usage hint in the status line: "{N} resets available ·
     expires … · **/reset usage limits openai**". There is no `/reset`, and
     the core has no banked-reset action either — the credits are
     display-only data from the provider's usage report. The hint promised
     an action the product does not have.
  Both strings are jcode hand-me-downs: the W3 rebrand renamed them but left
  the command references pointing at jcode's surface. **Corrected to state
  what is true and stop** — the tool reply keeps its true list, and the
  usage hint keeps the facts it has.
  **A guard now closes the class.** `every_command_a_user_facing_string_
  points_at_exists` scans the TUI's own strings for command references and
  checks each against the command table (public AND hidden) plus the handler
  registry. The scan is narrow ON PURPOSE — a slash plus a lowercase word
  sitting after a space, a bullet, a dash or a bracket, and not followed by
  "/" (which makes it a path) — and that narrowness is the difference between
  a guard and a permanently red test: the same scan without those two rules
  reports 84 tokens, 81 of them paths and test fixtures. With the rules it
  reports exactly one decision entry (`/tmp`, a path used in a doctest-style
  note). Reintroducing `/toolsets` fails the guard naming the file and line.

## CLOSED — the core had no context caps, a resume lost every tool turn, and a truncated answer lost its first half (found 2026-11-05, iter-1769)

- [x] **RT-225 (H, LOST CONTEXT) — three defects in the same loop: the caps
  the operator asked for did not exist, a resumed session lost the tool half
  of every turn, and a cut-off answer came back without its first half.**

  **1. The caps did not exist.** `[agent]` had no soft/hard cap of any kind:
  the preflight ladder fired at a fixed 80% of the window and the hard line
  was a fixed 95%. The operator's requirement — "hard-cap/soft-cap based on
  both number of tokens, and percentage of context-window", 350k soft by
  default, 400k hard, soft compacting at the turn end and hard compacting
  mid-stream — had nowhere to live. `[agent]` now carries four knobs
  (`context_soft_cap_tokens` 350 000, `context_soft_cap_percent` 0.80,
  `context_hard_cap_tokens` 400 000, `context_hard_cap_percent` 0.95) and
  BOTH axes bind: the smaller wins, so a 1M window compacts at 350k and
  never exceeds 400k, while a 128k window keeps the old 80%/95% behaviour.
  The soft cap IS the preflight threshold, and crossing it FORCES the
  compaction ladder to run — without that force the 350k cap would have been
  dead under a 1M window, because the ladder is otherwise gated on the
  prompt-cache bust permission (85%). The hard cap is checked BEFORE EVERY
  provider call, so a turn that grows past it mid-turn compacts the request
  list instead of sending an over-budget request; a context that cannot be
  compacted under the cap fails typed (`ContextExhausted`) instead of hitting
  a provider 400. The compaction rewrites the REQUEST list, never the durable
  transcript — a resumed session still has its whole history.
  Pinned by `crates/operant-core/tests/context_caps.rs`: the soft cap
  compacts at the turn boundary, a history UNDER the soft cap is not
  compacted (the control), and a turn that grows past the hard cap mid-turn
  compacts before the next provider call. Both cap tests are mutation-
  checked: disabling the mid-turn enforcement fails the hard-cap case, and
  disabling the soft-cap trigger fails the soft-cap case.

  **2. A resumed session lost every tool turn.** Three separate holes:
  `row_to_message` accepted only user and assistant rows, so every persisted
  TOOL row was dropped on rehydration; tool results were persisted through
  the short writer that carries no `tool_call_id`, so a resumed assistant
  tool request became an orphan and the request builder stripped the whole
  tool turn; and assistant messages went through the short writer too, which
  drops the reasoning and the finish reason. The transcript was also written
  TWICE: the core persists the user message and every assistant message, and
  the gateway wrote the same two rows again — so every turn showed the
  operator's message and the bot's answer twice. The core now owns the
  transcript (one row per message, the user row written exactly once even on
  a retried turn) and the gateway's duplicate writes are gone. Pinned by
  `crates/operant-core/tests/session_transcript.rs` (one user row, one
  assistant row, with the right content) and by the tool-pair rehydration
  case in `tests/agent_session_isolation.rs`.

  **3. A cut-off answer came back without its first half.** The
  `finish_reason="length"` path injected a bare "continue" prompt: the model
  could not see what it had already written (so it restarted) and the result
  carried only the continuation's text — the first half was dropped on the
  floor. The cut-off text now rides the continuation prompt and is prepended
  to the final answer. The strengthened case in
  `tests/loop_recovery_paths.rs` asserts both halves in the result and the
  partial output in the continuation request.

  **The wrap-up, the same class.** The grace summary — the LAST call of a
  budget-exhausted turn, the one that produced the operator's "⚠️ Turn ended
  early — the wrap-up ran out of room mid-summary" notice — was neither
  added to the conversation nor persisted, and a streaming failure escaped
  through `?` with a raw transport error, past the turn diagnostics and the
  error event. The summary is now continued when the provider cuts it off
  (bounded, the generic incomplete-response recovery), kept in the
  conversation and the transcript, and a failed wrap-up reports through the
  same diagnostics every other turn failure uses. Pinned by two new cases in
  `tests/grace_output_gate.rs`.

  The generic mechanism here is jcode's bounded response recovery (an
  incomplete response gets a continuation, capped), NOT its TODO-specific
  "poke": the poke's policy is TODO-shaped and was deliberately not ported.

## CLOSED — the TUI's context numbers were the wrong numbers, and a session boundary could wipe a live session (found 2026-11-05, iter-1769)

- [x] **RT-226 (M, WRONG NUMBER + RACE) — the context overlay showed the
  session's cumulative SPEND as the live context occupancy, the session
  totals showed the CURRENT turn's output, and `/clear`/`/new` could wipe a
  session a cancelled task was still writing into.**

  **The numbers.** `context_used_tokens` accumulated the turn totals of every
  request, so the context overlay painted "the window is full" after one long
  turn on a 200k window. It now holds the prompt the provider just billed —
  the live occupancy — which is the same figure the token-warning logic
  already used. `total_session_tokens()` returned `(accumulated spend, the
  CURRENT turn's output)`, so the "session: Nk in, Nk out" line changed on
  every turn and never described the session; it is now the session's
  cumulative input and output. Every session boundary (`/clear`, `/new`, a
  session switch) resets the per-session counters through ONE helper — a
  counter that survives the boundary labels the new session with the old
  session's numbers.

  **The race.** `/stop` clears `is_streaming` IMMEDIATELY, while the
  cancelled agent task keeps committing its tail for a moment. The
  clear/new/switch drain was gated on `!is_streaming` alone, so a boundary
  command that landed in that window wiped the session the tail was still
  writing into. The gate now also waits for the task itself
  (`agent_task_handle`), and the command stays pending until it is done.

  **The denominator.** The configured `[agent] context_window` is now the
  window every surface reports: a custom alias (`large-stack`) showed 200k
  in the TUI while the core ran with the configured 1M, because the display
  preferred the models.dev/provider table over the configuration.

  Pinned by four cases in `crates/operant-cli/src/tui/app/tests.rs`: the
  overlay shows the prompt occupancy, the session totals are cumulative, a
  session boundary resets the counters, and a boundary waits for the agent
  task. Each is mutation-sensitive by construction (the old accumulation,
  the old gate and the missing reset each fail their own case).

- [x] **RT-224 (M, FALSE HELP) — one chord, two features.** The keybinding

  | `Alt+Up` / `Alt+Down` | "scroll transcript up/down a page" | scrolls **20 rows** |
  | `Ctrl+Up` / `Ctrl+Down` | "scroll transcript up/down" | scrolls **3 rows** |

  Ctrl+X and Alt+P, whose Prompt rows merely worded their action differently

  pinned description — a shape a stale second copy cannot fail, which is
  exactly why the stale rows survived. It now requires **every** such row to

  Ctrl+T Prompt row fails it by name and context ("chord Ctrl+t is catalogued
